**Decision.** The edge's `run/acquirejob` reads the job row, its run, the repository's owner (`RepoOwner`), the owner's login and `Authz` (which name the repository), and the job's secrets and variables before it asks the shard to commit `Acquired`. A failure of any of them now answers 503 and commits nothing, and the log names the read that failed; a job or run the shard does not hold answers 404, as the shard's own acquire does, so the runner drops it rather than retrying (`acquire_config` in `workers/edge/src/actions.rs`, over an `AcquireReads` trait the edge and the test both implement; `repo_named_why` in `workers/edge/src/api.rs` names the failed login or `Authz` read). Before, only the secrets read did: a failure before it gave `None`, and the edge acquired with an empty `github.repository` and no secrets or variables.

**Why.** In BF-60's rerun (run 1966284) job 1966290's acquire answered 200 with an empty repository, and the runner failed the job at "Prepare workflow directory" with `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'repoFullName')` (`decisions/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`, F79). The same branch could start a job that needs secrets without them, which F77's rule forbids (`design/SHARED.md`, "Actions", Who decrypts). A 503 is the answer the runner retries: actions/runner v2.338.2 retries `GetJobMessageAsync` up to 5 times, 5 to 15 s apart, on anything but 404, 409, and 422, and then keeps polling [doc: `RunServer.cs`, `RunnerService.RetryRequest`, `Runner.cs`]. The job stays `Assigned`, so the broker resends it after `RESEND_AFTER` and its lease returns it to the queue.

**Beat.** (a) Retrying the failed read on the edge before answering: it holds the runner's request and only narrows the window, and the runner already retries. (b) Answering 404 or 422: the runner drops the job, which then waits out its lease with no runner. (c) Acquiring without the name and letting the runner fail the job: the bug itself.

**Evidence.** `an_acquire_whose_repository_read_fails_is_refused_never_sent_without_a_name_or_secrets` (`workers/edge/src/actions.rs`): each of the five reads, failed in turn, refuses the acquire as retryable naming it, no later read is made, and a job the shard does not hold is refused as gone; plants 55 to 58 put main's empty-name fallback back at the reads and plant 59 retries a missing job, all caught. `an_acquire_answered_503_leaves_the_job_assigned_for_a_resend_and_its_lease_requeues_it` (`crates/actions/tests/gates.rs`): after a 503 the job is still `Assigned`, the broker's next pick after `RESEND_AFTER` is `Resend` of the same job, and at the lease end the job is `Queued`, not failed.

**Flip.** A runner release that drops a job on a 503 from `acquirejob`, which would argue for answering the acquire only once every read has been retried on the edge; or a measured run where these 503s keep a job past its lease, which would argue for (a) on top.

### `f80-alarm-start`: a hosted runner's Sandbox starts its own process from its alarm, 2026-11-17

**Decision.** A `graft-runners` pass registers the runner and calls the Sandbox's `arm` (`workers/runners/entry.mjs`), which names the Sandbox, sets `keepAlive`, stores the start (the command and the JIT config) once under one storage key, schedules `launchRunner` on the Sandbox's alarm, and returns. The alarm (`workers/runners/launch.mjs`) starts the process unless `getProcess("runner")` finds it, so a retried alarm or a second `arm` starts nothing twice. It tries again every 10 s while placement fails and begins no try 6 minutes after the arm, so the last start lands before `HOSTED_IDLE` (600 s) and a runner that never started goes stale and is deleted instead. Once the process starts, or the runner is destroyed, it overwrites the stored start, dropping the JIT config. `destroy` closes the start first, and a start that lands after a close destroys its container. `launchRunner` never throws: `@cloudflare/containers` 0.3.x's `alarm()` logs a scheduled callback's throw and deletes its row, so a throw would drop the start for good. Every error, a storage read included, schedules the next try, and past the give-up a try only closes the start (lead's SDK review, 2026-11-17; `launchRunner` never throws, `f80-launch-nothrow`).

**Why.** F80: a delivery pass runs in `ctx.wait_until`, cut 30 s after the 202 [doc: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/context/], and a cold burst's placement waited p50 77.5 s (max 179 s) after the runner registered. Runs 1966284 and 1966233 cut 16 and 23 passes mid-start (`tests/m4/results/m4-wp4.md`, "Sandbox placement errors"). Run 1966284's runner 1704490 (Sandbox `55e4e998`, first called at 04:36:29Z, in the burst) never opened a session or made any install request, and was deleted stale at 04:46:38Z, about 610 s later; its Sandbox was destroyed 0.3 s after [measured, the edge's and the runner account's Workers Logs: the three stale deletes match the three Sandbox destroys to the second]. So a cut start held a cap slot for `HOSTED_IDLE`. An alarm handler has 15 minutes of wall time [doc: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/, "Durable Object alarm handlers"], runs at least once, retries a thrown handler up to 6 times from 2 s, and runs one at a time per object [doc: https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/]. One start try waits at most the SDK's 150 s transport budget, so a 180 s placement takes two tries inside one alarm. The Containers base class already arms that alarm on every start try and runs due `schedule` rows inside it, so the start adds no new loop.

**Beat.** (a) Pacing the starts: F80 found no published start-rate limit, and the SDK's own retries make the rate errors. (b) Awaiting the start before the 202: it holds the App's delivery open up to 2.5 minutes. (c) Moving the start to the 5-minute sweep or a Queue consumer (F80's candidate 2): it moves the cut to another limit and delays a delivery-prompted start by up to a sweep. (d) Retrying the start from the next pass: the runner keeps its slot until then, and a pass cannot tell a slow start from a lost one.

**Evidence.** `workers/runners/tests/launch.test.mjs` (`node --test 'workers/runners/tests/*.test.mjs'`, in CI) runs a fake Sandbox on virtual time with run 1966284's burst placement waits. Delivery passes are cut at 30 s, alarms at 15 minutes and retried. Its tests: 20 cold starts each start one process and no pass is cut; a crash after the start and a second delivery start no second process; a destroy before or during the wait leaves no process; a Sandbox never placed closes before `HOSTED_IDLE` and starts nothing after. On main's rule (the pass starts the process itself, plant 60), every pass that waits on placement is cut and its runner never starts. Plants 60 to 68 (`tests/m4/wp4/plant.py`) are caught; 68 lets a storage error escape `launchRunner`, as main at a29a57d2 did, and `a start whose storage read fails is tried again, not dropped with its row` fails on it. Run hosted on 2026-11-17: cold-burst run 1966335 after the class sat idle 8 hours cut 0 delivery passes (run 1966284: 16), opened 50 sessions for 50 registrations, and logged one `launched` line on each of 50 Sandboxes, none twice (`tests/m4/results/m4-wp4.md`, "F80 cold-burst check on the alarm start").

**Flip.** A hosted cold burst in which an alarm-started process starts twice or after its runner's delete, or a delivery pass is still cut mid-start; or the Sandbox SDK starting a process from its own alarm-safe API, which would replace `launch.mjs`.

### `pr-trigger`: `ActionsTrigger` starts `pull_request` runs at the current test merge, 2026-11-17

**Decision.** `ActionsTrigger` (`workers/site/src/actions_trigger.rs`, pure half `crates/actions/src/trigger.rs`) also starts runs for a pull request's `opened`, `synchronize`, and `reopened`, read from each committed entry as `Webhooks` reads them (`graftyard_git::hooks::webhooks`). For each event, concurrently, it asks for the pull request's test merge (`crate::prsync::demand`, `MergeCause::Dispatch`) when the fold has none of the current head, reads the merge from the leader's fold, and, for a clean merge, commits each matching workflow's `CreateRun` with `head_sha` the merge commit and `head_ref` `refs/pull/N/merge`. The latest merge of the current head counts at whatever base tip it was computed on, since that is what `refs/pull/N/merge` holds. A conflicting merge starts no run. A merge the budget shed is asked again inside its event, up to 4 times 2 s apart; after that the event is carried to the next round, as below. An event whose head has already moved on still gets its run, at the merge current when the run is created; the dispatch log line counts it as `superseded`. The run key names `refs/pull/N/merge` after the workflow path, as a `merge_group` run's names its queue ref, so one entry that moves several pull requests' heads starts a run for each; such a `CreateRun` is format 0x15.4 (`ACTIONS_FORMAT_PULL_REQUEST`). The scan runs only where a site day set `GRAFTYARD_PR_TRIGGER` to `1`.

- **Guard for first scans.** An entry more than an hour old (`PR_REPLAY_MS`) starts no `pull_request` run. Where a site day first sets the variable, `ActionsTrigger`'s cursor may sit far behind the log, and without the guard its first scan would start a run for every push it ever took. The guard is install-side: GitHub's trigger never replays, and a client sees no difference for any event it just sent.
- **Format order.** The leader refuses a command whose format its release does not read (`crates/raft/src/member/leader.rs`, `take_record` and `commit`), and a follower refuses such an entry (`crates/raft/src/member/log.rs`, `verify`). So: first a site day ships the 0x15.4 reader to every member of all three sites, with `GRAFTYARD_PR_TRIGGER` unset, so nothing sends 0x15.4. Then a later site day sets `GRAFTYARD_PR_TRIGGER=1`, the same order as `GRAFTYARD_APP_HOOKS` after 32.24. A site day resets every member, so after the first one every Actions shard member reads 0x15.4 before any `ActionsTrigger` can send it.
- **Dispatch time**, which B0-35 bounds: from the acknowledgment of the push or pull request entry to `RunCreated` committed on the Actions shard. The site logs it per event from the entry's `at` (`actions dispatch ... in Nms`), and `tests/am1/rest/a1.mjs --workflow` measures it from the driver's acknowledgment to the run listed by the admin runs route.

- **Carried items (F84, 2026-11-17, after the hosted run).** A round tries each item once: each queue ref its entries built, each pull request event, and each item carried from the last round. An item it could not finish (its merge still shed after 4 asks, or a shard read or `CreateRun` that failed) is carried alone to the next round, `RETRY_MS` (5 s) later, and the rest of the batch counts as done. So no failure reruns a batch. The cursor commits at the index just below the oldest carried item's entry (`graftyard_actions::trigger::settle`), so a new leader, whose scan starts from the committed cursor, rescans that entry and loses no event, and the run key keeps a rescan from creating a run twice. A pull request event still not done `PR_REPLAY_MS` (1 h) after its entry is given up and logged `unmerged`: by then the first-scan guard would start none either. A queue ref is never given up, as before. A round whose cursor commit fails owes it, and the next round commits it. The carried list lives in the leader's memory: a new leader or a member reset loses it and rescans from the cursor, which is no later than the oldest carried entry. A round logs a shed event `pending`, and `tests/m4/wp4/dispatchlog.py` counts the first `pending` as its first try's `unmerged`.

**Why.** B0-35's last line, Actions dispatch p99, had no run to measure: main started no `pull_request` run, and push and pull request runs came only from the admin dispatch route ("M4-WP3: BF-37's merge queue setting and `ActionsTrigger` for `merge_group`", whose flip names this). GitHub creates a run for every default-type event at the event's merge commit, and the run's `GITHUB_SHA` is the "Last merge commit on the `GITHUB_REF` branch" with `GITHUB_REF` `refs/pull/PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER/merge`; a pull request with a merge conflict starts no workflow [doc: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows, `pull_request`]. Dropping a superseded event's run would change what a client sees (lead's review, 2026-11-17). DESIGN's Shape already has dispatch call `demand` (`TestMerge`), whose only caller this is. The old run key `(chain, index, workflow)` would refuse every pull request of an entry but the first.

**Beat.** (a) Skipping an event whose head has moved on: fewer runs, but GitHub runs it, so a client would see a different run list. (b) A run at the head commit on `refs/pull/N/head`: not GitHub's `GITHUB_SHA`. (c) A separate consumer and cursor for `pull_request`: a second scan of the same log for the same reads. (d) Sending 0x15.4 from the same site day that ships its reader: one member of a shard on the old release would refuse every entry after it.

**Evidence.** `crates/actions/tests/pr_trigger.rs`, on a real repository group and Actions shard: one entry that moves two pull requests starts a run for each at its own merge (fails on main's key, plant 69); a conflict starts none and a missing merge is pending (plants 71, 72); a superseded event runs at the current merge (plant 72); the hour guard (plant 74); a shard that does not read 0x15.4 refuses the run (plant 70). Plants 69 to 75 (`tests/m4/wp4/plant.py`). Fold size: 3,000 single-job `pull_request` runs encode the Actions fold to 1.38 MB, under the fold row's 2 MB, measured in memory with the B0-35 workflow.

**Base tip (2026-11-17, before the hosted run).** The merged rule counted a merge only at the current base tip, and failed the round on any event still without one. B0-35 moves the base every 6 s, so an event could read its fresh merge as stale once the base moved, and the test-merge budget shed 6,043 of 6,750 merges in LM-1 round 5 (BUILD-PLAN, round 5), so a dispatch merge is often shed. Either failed the round, which reruns its whole batch, so with one such event in nearly every 200-entry batch the cursor would never move [inference, from those rates; found reading the code before site day 51]. `a_merge_at_an_older_base_still_counts` fails on that rule (plant 76).

**Carried items, why.** B0-35's run `mwl642gm` had 0 of 1,198 events `unmerged` at the end, but only because failed rounds reran their batches: 103 (8.6%) were `unmerged` on their first try, and 278 events were logged twice [measured, `tests/m4/results/m4-wp4.md`, "B0-35 with Actions dispatch on graft-m4a"]. Main's rule had two faults. An event given up after 4 asks lost its run whenever no rerun followed. And a failed round reran all of its up to 200 entries' events, so a single shed merge cost the whole batch's reads and `CreateRun` calls again. Carrying the item fixes both: the event waits up to an hour without depending on a rerun, and nothing done is redone. It beat (e) failing the round (main before `b035-base-tip`: the cursor stalls behind any shed merge); (f) a per-event retry with no cap (an event whose merge never commits would hold the cursor forever; the hour matches the replay guard); (g) moving the cursor past a carried event (a new leader would skip it, losing its run, which plant 78 shows); (h) a persisted carried list (a row write per shed event, where the cursor below the oldest one already makes a new leader rescan it). Evidence: `a_shed_merge_is_carried_alone_and_the_cursor_waits_below_it` in `crates/actions/tests/pr_trigger.rs` fails on main's rule (plant 79) and on a batch rerun (plant 82); plants 78 to 82. Hosted: not run; it waits for B0-35's rerun, after an A1 row holds commits at 500 agents.

**Flip.** A hosted run in which a `pull_request` event starts no run or two, or starts one at a commit other than the merge current at its creation; GHES behaviour that differs from the cited doc; or a `paths` filter, which needs the merge's changed paths (not built: `paths` passes, as for a new branch).

### `trigger-stream`: `ActionsTrigger` runs as a stream, and dispatch merges go first in the turn, 2026-11-19

**Status.** Approved by the lead (T-01a17bda) after B0-35 m54, code-only, on branch `dispatch-tail`. It ships on a site day, with no format change. B0-35's rerun waits on it and on LM-1's B0-33 work on the shed reads behind m54's `suspect` burst.

**Decision.**
- **A stream, not rounds** (`graftyard_actions::trigger::Stream`, host `workers/site/src/actions_trigger.rs`). Each queue ref and pull request event starts as soon as its entry is read and a slot is free, up to `IN_FLIGHT_MAX` (100 [guess]) at once, and each ends on its own. When one ends, the host starts the next item and reads more entries. It reads the next `BATCH` only while every item read has started and a slot is free, so the items waiting for a slot are at most one batch's.
- **The cursor rule is `settle`'s.** The cursor may commit just below the oldest item not done, whether it is queued, running, or waiting to be tried again (`low_water`), or at the last entry read when every item is done. A new leader rescans from the committed cursor, so a crash replays each item not done and never skips one, and the shard's run key makes a replay create nothing twice. It commits at most every `CURSOR_EVERY_MS` (5 s [guess]) while items end, so a stream of events costs one cursor entry an interval, not one per event.
- **Tried again alone.** An item that ended `Again` (its merge still shed after `DEMAND_TRIES` asks, a read or `CreateRun` failed) starts again `RETRY_MS` (5 s) later, ahead of newer items, and is given up as `unmerged` an hour after its entry, as under rounds.
- **Dispatch first in the turn** (`graftyard_git::prsync::MergeTurn`). When a network's turn frees, a waiting `Dispatch` merge goes before waiting head pushes and GETs, as `MergeCause` says, unless `DISPATCH_STREAK_MAX` (4 [guess]) dispatch merges just ran in a row and another merge waits. Within a cause it is first come, first served. A merge that leaves the line while the turn is handed to it passes the turn on.
- **Timing in the log line.** Each `actions dispatch` line ends with `wait Nms demand Nms reads Nms create Nms`: the wait from the entry to the try's start, the test merge's asks, the workflow `tree`/`blob` reads, and the `CreateRun` calls.

**Why.** B0-35 m54 failed dispatch at p99 120 s. The tail was the rounds: a round ran its batch's events together and ended only with its slowest, p50 42 s and p99 75 s, and an entry that committed during it waited for the next one, p50 26.2 s and p99 96.9 s. The slowest 1% waited 119 s on average for their round against 31 s inside it. Each ask inside a round waited in one turn shared by every cause, up to 371 merges long, so 1 ask took p50 18.1 s and 2 asks 33.3 s against 10.2 s with none [measured, `tests/m4/results/m4-wp4.md`, "B0-35 rerun on graft-m4a after site day 54"]. The leader changes widened the tail in their minutes, but the other minutes' p99 was still 92 s. With both changes the expected entry-to-run is about the 0-ask time, p50 about 10 s and p99 about 15 s on m54's load [inference]. The timing split is there to attribute those 10 s, which m54 could not.

**What it beat.**
- **Shorter rounds** (a smaller `BATCH`). A round still ends with its slowest event, and one shed merge holds it for four asks.
- **Rounds that do not wait for a slow event**, starting the next round while carried events run. That is a stream with two names for one state, and the round's cursor would need the stream's rule anyway.
- **A separate dispatch turn** that runs beside head pushes. It would run two merges at once on one network, which `budgeted`'s overrun bound forbids: each merge is admitted only once the one before was charged.
- **Strict priority for dispatch.** Under a constant stream of dispatch, head pushes and GETs would never run.

**Evidence.** `crates/actions/tests/pr_trigger.rs`:
- `a_stream_commits_the_runs_rounds_commit_and_its_cursor_never_passes_an_unfinished_event` runs ten events both ways, with one pull request's merge shed at first. It compares the committed `CreateRun`s, by workflow, ref, commit, and entry, and checks the cursor against every running and retried item.
- `a_slow_event_holds_one_slot_and_the_cursor_waits_below_it`: with a cap of two and the first event never ending, the other nine run beside it, and the cursor waits below it.

`crates/git/tests/agent_load.rs`, `dispatch_goes_first_in_the_turn_and_the_rest_never_starve`:
- a dispatch merge behind queued head pushes and a GET runs first;
- under 21 dispatch merges, no more than four run in a row while another waits;
- a dropped waiter passes the turn on.

Plants 99 to 105 (`tests/m4/wp4/plant.py`): a cursor past an unfinished event (99), a retried item that does not hold it (100), no cap (101), a retry dropped (102), a first-come turn (103), unbounded dispatch (104), and a dropped waiter that keeps the turn (105). Hosted: not run.

**Flip.**
- A hosted B0-35 row where entry-to-run's p99 still comes from waiting for a slot (the `wait` field) rather than the try: raise `IN_FLIGHT_MAX`, or move dispatch off the leader's isolate.
- An isolate memory error with 100 items in flight.
- A row where head-push merges shed `late` because dispatch takes the turn: lower `DISPATCH_STREAK_MAX`.
- An event that starts no run or two (the `pr-trigger` flip).

### `r29-commit-heartbeat`: an idle leader tells each follower its last commit once, and a purge wakes the group first, 2026-11-19

**Status.** Code-only, on branch `r29-commit-heartbeat`, not deployed. The Raft half ships on a site day; the purge route's probe is edge code and ships on an edge day. Answers R29 (`decisions/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`).

**Decision.**
- **A commit round** (`tick_leader`, `crates/raft/src/member/leader.rs`). The leader keeps, per follower, the commit its latest answered round told it: the lower of the commit that round carried and the index the follower matched (`Lead::told`, from `Lead::telling`). A follower that holds every entry but was told less than the leader's commit gets one more AppendEntries once the last round to it is `CALL_DEADLINE` old. A busy group's next entry carries the commit, so it sends nothing extra; an idle leader that told every follower sends nothing at all, as before.
- **The purge route wakes the group** (`workers/edge/src/purge.rs`). Before it reads the members' statuses, it sends one `{"q": {"probe": true}}` read per chain through `call_opt`, whose lookup reports a leaderless group with `suspect` and so starts its election, as `tier-off-elect` does for a group read only by dumps. A chain with no group answers `None` and is not created.

**Why.** On graft-m4a's 65567 (2026-11-18) `#1#f0` held commit 5044, with both followers at commit 5043 and last 5044, all three followers in term 26 with no leader; the gate refused `NoTombstone` for 4.5 minutes, until one `/campaign` made `#1#f0` lead and its next append carried 5044 [measured, R29]. In memory the first half reproduces with no leader loss: after one commit and 30 idle `CALL_DEADLINE`s, the leader holds commit 4 and both followers commit 3 (`an_idle_leader_tells_its_followers_the_last_commit_once` fails on main f6123990). The leader sends a follower an append only while it is behind or a read, transfer, or campaign waits, and a follower learns a commit only from an append. The second half is why 65567 also had no leader: `keep_led` campaigns only while `Family::needs_leader` holds (split or archive due), and nothing reads a deleted repository. With the commit round the followers learn the commit about 1 s after it, while the host's ticker still runs (`ACTIVE_FOR_MS`, 3 s), so a leader lost later leaves nothing to tell [inference]. A leader lost inside that second still can, and the probe covers the one reader that needs it.

**What it beat.**
- **Treating "told below commit" as `behind`, every `CALL_DEADLINE`, with no told record.** An idle leader then beats forever, which breaks `suspect`'s "a report counts only while the leader makes no progress" (plant 108 fails four `leadership` tests that way).
- **The commit round at once, after each commit.** A busy group sends an empty round beside every entry; waiting `CALL_DEADLINE` lets the next entry carry it.
- **`keep_led` counting an uncommitted follower as work due.** It would campaign every leaderless group whose follower is one commit short, deleted or not, for a fact only a purge reads, and a follower cannot tell a commit it was never told from an entry that never committed.
- **The purge gate accepting a member one commit short.** The tombstone is the purge's evidence; the gate must see it applied.

**Evidence.**
- `an_idle_leader_tells_its_followers_the_last_commit_once` (`crates/raft/tests/scenarios.rs`): fails on main; checks nothing leaves inside `CALL_DEADLINE`, both followers reach the leader's commit just after it, and then five more idle `CALL_DEADLINE`s send nothing.
- Tests that assumed an idle leader sends nothing after `Cluster::sync`: `sync` now runs one more `CALL_DEADLINE`, so a report after it is still late; two `leadership` tests and `a_voter_is_pipelined_unless_its_link_is_lossy` count the commit round's time. `bf68_eu_documents_stay_in_eu_shards_a_killed_shard_reports_incomplete_until_its_rebuild` (`crates/api/tests/activity_gates.rs`) waited only for 13 documents to be indexed, and a comment adds none; with followers learning commits sooner the count reached 13 at 1.4 s instead of 2.9 s, before the comment's entry was indexed, so it now waits for the comment too. The simulator sweeps pass unchanged.
- Plants 106 to 108 (`tests/m4/wp4/plant.py`): main's rule (106), the round at once (107), and an answer never counted as told (108). 3 of 3 caught.
- `a_fresh_leaders_first_idle_period_sends_one_round_per_follower_then_nothing` (`crates/raft/tests/scenarios.rs`): a new leader has no `told` entry, so its first idle period sends each follower one empty round after `CALL_DEADLINE`, carrying its term's commit, and then nothing for five more; it checks this after a new group's first election and after a hand-off, with the leader still leading.
- The long sweep (`RAFT_SEEDS=2000 RAFT_STEPS=10000 RAFT_HISTORY=...`, `crates/raft/tests/sim.rs`, `long_sweep`) on the branch merged with main 03404ace (7a4b1c05): exit 0 in 920 s. Porcupine (`-seg 2000`): `hist.jsonl` Ok on 146,836 operations, `hist.jsonl.gray` Ok on 2,335,345, `hist.jsonl.live` Ok on 5,287,143. Longest stretches with a healthy quorum and nothing completing: HARSH 14.7 s (seed 10439), GRAY 28.5 s (11893), live 25.2 s (13897), under the 30 s bound; main 03404ace's own sweep gave 16.8 s, 24.2 s (11076), and 29.1 s (10681) [measured].
- The GRAY tail, seed by seed over the same 2,000 seeds: branch mean 8,880 ms, p99 21.5 s, 33 seeds over 20 s and 2 over 25 s; main mean 8,769 ms, p99 20.4 s, 22 over 20 s and 0 over 25 s. 594 seeds moved by more than 5 s, 294 longer and 300 shorter, and seed 11893 itself is 13.9 s on main [measured]. That fits the timing churn `tests/m0/results/read-rounds.md` found (673 of 2,000 seeds moved by more than 5 s), not a stall the commit round causes [inference].
- **The purge probe, hosted on edge day 28 (graft-m4a, 2026-11-19), with a leader [measured].** `workers/edge` has no harness for the route's bindings, so no test drives it. Scratch repository `m3org/r29-probe-56` (65570), created at 18:02:04Z and deleted with 204: its group had a leader before each first-pass call (`#1#f0`, term 2, all three at commit 16 to 28). The first pass answered 409 "A member is in a group change" twice (the create's group change, timing), then 200 at 18:03:54Z: 19 objects, 4 members retired. The second pass at 18:10:41Z answered 200, 0 objects, with every first-generation member already retired (no group). No status read answered 503, the gate decided on its facts, and no `/campaign` or `suspect` ran in the window [measured: `tests/m4/raw/wp4/purge35.jsonl`, Workers Logs]. The route's probe half is no longer [unverified]; waking a leaderless group with a committed tombstone stays [inference], because a product build cannot make a group leaderless on purpose.

**Cost.** At most one empty AppendEntries per follower per commit, and only when the group commits less often than once per `CALL_DEADLINE` [inference]. A down follower already got a re-send every `CALL_DEADLINE` while behind, so it adds none there.

**Flip.**
- A hosted row where a group that commits about once a second or less shows AppendEntries per entry above 2 per follower, or leader CPU from empty rounds: send the round on the lease extension's schedule instead.
- A long sweep whose GRAY or live half breaks the 30 s bound, or a second sweep that again puts more GRAY seeds over 20 s than main (here 33 against 22): find whether the commit round renews a gray leader's promises.
- A purge refused `NoTombstone` again after a second call on a group with a committed tombstone: the probe did not wake it, so wake it from the member (`keep_led` for a tombstoned repository).

### `r23-runnerbox`: hosted runners start on one `RunnerBox` class with the platform's `ctx.container`, so a 10% version runs its own image, 2026-11-19

**Status.** Code-only, on branch `r23-runnerbox`, not deployed. Answers R23 (`decisions/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`). Option (a) of the R23 design, approved by the operator through the lead thread on 2026-11-19.

**Decision.**
- **One class, one application.** `RunnerBox` (`workers/runners/entry.mjs`, start logic in `workers/runners/box.mjs`) extends `DurableObject` and uses no Sandbox SDK. It runs on one container application created with the `durable_object` scheduling policy, which takes no image, instance type, or `max_instances` (`cli/src/runners.rs`, `ensure_apps`). Each `graft-runners` version names the image in its metadata, `containers: [{ class_name: "RunnerBox", images: { runner: <digest> } }]`, as the site script's `GitShard` does.
- **The start.** A pass calls `arm(name, instance, jit)`, which stores the start once and sets the object's alarm. The alarm calls `ctx.container.start({ image: images.runner, instance, enableInternet: true, env: { JIT }, entrypoint })` unless the container is running, with `entrypoint` `/bin/sh -c 'exec /home/runner/run.sh --jitconfig "$JIT"'`, so the runner is PID 1 and its exit stops the container. A start that the platform refuses ("no container instance") is tried again every 10 s and gives up 6 minutes after the arm, before `HOSTED_IDLE`. A start that ends within 3 s logs `runner exited within 3 s … image X`; one that runs sets the inactivity timeout to 6 h and logs `launched … image X`. A destroy wins over a start in flight. F80's shape is kept.
- **Routing.** The Worker starts on `RunnerBox` while the version's `RUNNER_BOX_ON` variable is "1" (`runners.json` `runner_box`), and on the legacy `SandboxStd3`/`SandboxStd4` otherwise. `destroy` asks `RunnerBox` first, which answers false for a runner it never held, then the legacy class.
- **Releases.** Each stands alone and rolls back alone.
  - **M1** (`graftyard runners init` on the `v1` account, a whole deploy): adds the `RunnerBox` class (migration `v1` to `v2`) and its application, and removes nothing; `RUNNER_BOX_ON` stays unset, so nothing starts on it. Rollback: none needed for behavior, since the class is unused; a class cannot be removed without a new migration, so it stays.
  - **M2** (`graftyard runners upgrade` with `runner_box: true`): the version at 10% for a day starts its runners on `RunnerBox` with its own image, then 100%. No application rolls. Rollback: deploy the previous version at 100%; boxes already armed finish their jobs, and `destroy` still reaches runners on either class.
  - **M3**, only after M2 has run a day at 100% with no stale runners: a whole deploy with migration `v3` (`deleted_classes: ["SandboxStd3", "SandboxStd4"]`), then delete their two applications. Rollback: there is no class rollback, which is why M3 has its gate; to recover, deploy M2's code without the legacy fallback, or re-add the classes under a new migration.
- **Concurrency.** With no `max_instances`, a cold burst is bounded by: `decide`'s per-owner cap across passes (a registration past 20 gets 409 and the pass moves to the next label); `RUNNER_VCPU_STOP_PCT` within a pass, counted from every registered runner (the start is skipped, counted in `vcpu_stopped`, and logged); and the account's vCPU limit (placement is refused, the box retries, then gives up and the registration goes stale). Overlapping passes each count only what they read, so between owners the account limit is the backstop.

**Why.** R23: a `default`-policy application holds one image, so `runners upgrade`'s 10% version started its Sandboxes on the old image, and a bad image reached every runner at once at the 100% roll. The pinned `@cloudflare/containers` 0.3.7 builds the start config from four fields only and cannot pass `image` or `instance` (`container.js:1317-1378`), and Cloudflare's guide says the `Container` class does not support the `durable_object` policy [doc: containers/guides/migrate-to-durable-object-scheduling-policy]. The policy is fixed at creation [doc: containers/configuration/scheduling-policy], so a new application is needed in any case. During a gradual deployment each object sees the image map of the version that runs it [doc], and running containers keep their startup image [measured, `tests/m0/results/container-survival.json`].

**What it beat.**
- **(b) Wrapping the Sandbox SDK's private `container`** in the `RunnerSandbox` constructor. It needs the same new application and all three releases, and a `^0.3.x` patch that renames the field or adds a second start site makes every start fail, or silently run the default image, with no compile error.
- **(c) No new application: rolling the existing applications at 10%, or alternating application pairs per release.** An application rollout replaces running containers, so it can kill jobs in flight, and an image rolled apart from the Worker version breaks the pairing between the runner image and the code that starts it.
- **Sandbox SDK 1.x.** It is a rewrite with no Sandbox class whose own example calls `ctx.container.start`, so it buys nothing over calling it directly.

**Evidence.**
- `workers/runners/tests/box.test.mjs` (`node --test 'workers/runners/tests/*.test.mjs'`), a fake account on virtual time. All of these fail on main, which has no `box.mjs`:
  - a 10% version starts its own image and the other 90% theirs;
  - a broken image at 10% logs one `exited within` line naming it, while the 90% launch;
  - placement refusals retry and a retried alarm starts none, with exactly one placed start;
  - the runner is PID 1 and its exit stops the container;
  - a cold burst of 16 on 20 vCPU never runs more than 20, and starts that outlast the give-up close;
  - a destroy during a refused or placed start wins.
- `a_cold_burst_is_bounded_by_the_cap_across_passes_and_the_vcpu_stop_within_one` (`workers/runners/src/control.rs`): one pass over three owners with 100 vCPU starts 35 (70 vCPU) and skips 25; four overlapping passes register exactly 20 per owner and no pass starts past its stop.
- CLI (`cli/src/runners.rs`): init creates `RunnerBox`'s application on `durable_object` with no image or cap and migrates `v1` to `v2`; on a `v1` account it adds only `RunnerBox`; a `runner_box` upgrade's version carries the image and `RUNNER_BOX`, and nothing rolls; upgrade refuses an account without `RunnerBox`.
- Plants 109 to 122 (`tests/m4/wp4/plant.py`), 14 of 14 caught. Plants 15, 16, and 18 to 20 still caught.
- **M1 and its cold-burst check, 2026-11-19** (`tests/m4/results/m4-wp4.md`, "R23: release M1 and the `RunnerBox` cold-burst check"). M1 ran: migration `v2` and the `durable_object` application exist, and `RUNNER_BOX_ON` is unset. The check stopped at its first start [measured]:
  - **A version upload needs image preparation.** A direct-API version whose image map names a pushed, digest-pinned image uploads, but on run 1712951 each of the 8 `ctx.container.start`s returned and its `monitor()` rejected in under a second with "Image not found … have created an application with it". Wrangler calls `POST /containers/image-preparations` until `READY` before such an upload. So the operator CLI now does it in one place for both CLIs: `Cf::put_script` and `Cf::upload_version` prepare every image a version's `containers` entries name, each once, polling every 2 s up to 15 minutes, and upload nothing if an image is refused or never ready, with an error naming it (`cli/src/cf.rs`, `prepare_image`). `graftyard sites` uploads `GitShard`'s `images.git` the same way and had the same gap, hidden because every site day so far deployed through Wrangler (R30). Tests: preparation before the upload, a prepared image in one call, pending polled to ready, never ready and refused upload nothing; plants 123 to 128, 6 of 6 caught.
  - **A failed start surfaces through `monitor()`, not as a throw from `start()`.** A refused placement for want of an instance was not reached and stays [unverified].
  - The variable was first named `RUNNER_BOX`, like the namespace binding, and the API refused the version (code 10053); it is `RUNNER_BOX_ON`.
  - **The rerun with the image prepared** (run 1712968): 8 of 8 containers launched 3 s after their arm, at `standard-3` or `standard-4` as each start asked, and every job succeeded. PID 1 was `/bin/bash /home/runner/run.sh` with no Sandbox server running, and each container stopped with exit 0 when its runner exited [measured]. Refused placement for want of capacity was not reached and stays [unverified].

**Flip.**
- M1's cold-burst check shows a refused placement that is neither a throw nor a "no container instance" rejection, or starts that place more than the account's vCPU: then cap starts in the box (a counter object) before M2.
- A canary whose bad image the by-image count missed: then gate the 100% run on `tests/m4/wp4/sandboxstarts.py`'s `by_image` in `runners upgrade` itself.
- The Containers platform adding an application-level instance cap to the `durable_object` policy: then set it as the legacy applications' `max_instances` did.

### `roll-up`: a bounded roll of a chain's oldest promoted packs, recorded as `Compacted` on the repository chain, 2026-11-16

**Status.** Approved by the operator after round 32's review, with the repository-chain form; built on branch `rollup` (G9), not deployed. Built: the fold and `verify`, the archive alarm's roll step (`log_archive::roll_plan`, `Step::Rolled`), the site's warm `/roll` through the promotion path, the container's `/roll`, the rehydrate's read of produced packs with its fallback to the consumed packs, the site variable `GRAFTYARD_ROLLUP` that gates every roll (`log_archive::rollup_enabled`: unset, the alarm sends no `/roll` and records no `Compacted`; a site day sets it to `1` only after `FormatsEnable` enabled 32.25, as R24's `GRAFTYARD_APP_HOOKS` waits for 32.24), and the deletion guard as a pure rule (`sweep::consumed_deletable`). Not built: the sweeper's deletion of consumed packs, which waits for that rule's shard answers (G9's remainder). DESIGN, Shape, `Promoted` and `rehydrate`, and Failure modes (pack buckets bad-deploy, git caches noisy-tenant) carry the rule; this entry carries the numbers.

**Decision.**
- **What rolls.** On one repository chain, the oldest run of promoted packs that no roll has consumed, in index order and consecutive (each `Promoted.from` is the last one's `to + 1`), stopping before the run's packs pass ROLL_IN_MAX bytes in, 2 GiB [guess, from the memory bound below]. A roll runs once that run reaches ROLL_IN_MAX, or once it holds ROLL_MIN_PACKS (8) packs and is older than a day [guess]. A rolled pack is never rolled again, so no roll's input grows past ROLL_IN_MAX and there is no second level. The roll is one complete pack of every object of its inputs.
- **Who writes it.** The repository group's archive alarm (`log_archive::step`), after promotion and archiving have nothing due, as a fourth step: it asks the chain's home shard, as a warm call (`promote-warm`: it starts no stopped shard), for `/roll` with the input packs' ids and checksums. The shard runs `pack-objects --stdin-packs --delta-base-offset` over exactly those packs, at nice 19, `pack.threads=2`, `pack.windowMemory=256m`, holding the repack's slot so a roll and a repack never run together. It streams the pack and its `.idx` back through the same path as a promotion (`PackStore::place_promoted`, a `/validate` on the same shard), and the leader commits `RepoEvent::Compacted { consumed, produced, from, to }` (`RepoEvent` tag 47, repository format 32.25; tag 46 and 32.24 are R24's `WorkflowJob`, M4-WP4) in an entry of its own, with a request id from the inputs' digests, so a re-sent step after a lost answer records nothing twice. The payload is SHARED's `NetworkEvent::Compacted { consumed, produced }` plus the index range the rolled promotions cover.
- **`decide`.** It accepts a `Compacted` only when every consumed pack is a committed `Promoted` pack of this chain not consumed before, the consumed ranges are consecutive and equal to `from..=to`, and `produced` is one stored pack. The fold keeps the list of (from, to, produced) rolls beside `promoted`.
- **The memory bound.** A roll's RSS is about 1.7 times its input bytes and its private memory about 0.6 times (table below). At ROLL_IN_MAX 2 GiB that is about 3.6 GB RSS, 1.3 GB private, beside a container's 12 GiB with the repack's 1.7 GB (`repack-keep-pack`) and clones, and it never runs beside the repack. A whole-network roll of 6.8 GB failed on this orb at 10.4 GB maxrss (killed), as round 23b's 8.6 GB said it would.
- **Rehydrate prefers a rolled pack.** `rehydrate_plan` drops every pack a committed `Compacted` consumed (`ChainLog::compactions` reads each chain's rolls from the `ranges` read), loads `produced` by its stored `.idx` as a promotion is loaded, and `skippable` treats a roll's `from..=to` as a promotion's range, so the pushed packs below it stay skipped. A roll whose produced pack has no `Committed` marker does not count: the shard loads its consumed packs instead, while they exist (below). Each counted roll's produced pack loads first, alone, oldest range first; one that does not load (no bucket copy matches its checksum, the container refuses it, or its bases are missing) is dropped for that run and reported (`Rehydrated::dropped_rolls`), and its consumed packs load in its place, which holds because nothing deletes them yet. A bad `.idx` alone falls back to `index-pack`, as a promotion's does. Tests: `a_roll_whose_produced_pack_does_not_load_falls_back_to_the_packs_it_consumed` fails without the fallback; `two_rolls_load_oldest_first_and_both_count`; `an_unset_rollup_variable_rolls_nothing`.
- **Deleting consumed packs.** A consumed pack and its `.idx` are deleted, then its `Committed` marker, by the sweeper only once all of: the `Compacted` is CONSUMED_KEEP (7 days) old; every shard holding the network (each warm site's first shard and its held pool slots) answers a warm `/status` with a cursor at or past the `Compacted`'s index, or holds no disk for it; and the network is not in a restore window that reads below the roll. A shard that cannot answer holds the deletion (`sweep::consumed_deletable`; the sweeper does not call it yet). Until deleted, consumed packs keep their markers, so the orphan rule never removes them early, and the filler skips them.

**Why.** On B0-34's network the cold warm reads 8.64 GB of stored packs at 104 to 132 MB/s, which with the platform's start (33 to 36 s) and the tail plus `/connected` (32 to 47 s) gives 150 to 158 s against DESIGN's 120 s (round 26). Under 120 s needs the stored packs read in about 39 to 54 s, so 4.1 to 7.1 GB at that rate (round 27b). Rolling promotions shrinks the bytes: 6-step promotions of B0-34's plan rolled 8 at a time come to 0.52 of their input, 16 at a time 0.42 (round 32). A re-promotion cannot shrink committed ranges (`check_promoted`), and more streams do not raise the total past the container's R2 rate (round 27b).

**Measured on B0-34's plan** (`tests/fanout/rollup/`, round 27's fixture: 33 complete 6-step promotions and the base, 6.80 GB; `pack-objects --stdin-packs` at nice 19 on 2 threads, `windowMemory=256m`, on 4 CPUs):

| promotions rolled | in | out | out/in | wall | CPU | maxrss | private |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 0.42 GB | 0.31 GB | 0.73 | 24 s | 31 s | 0.84 GB | 0.40 GB |
| 4 | 0.80 GB | 0.51 GB | 0.64 | 40 s | 58 s | 1.47 GB | 0.64 GB |
| 8 | 1.68 GB | 0.87 GB | 0.52 | 84 s | 124 s | 2.82 GB | 1.09 GB |
| 16 | 3.52 GB | 1.48 GB | 0.42 | 176 s | 263 s | 5.72 GB | 2.11 GB |
| 34 (all) | 6.80 GB | killed | | 302 s | 481 s | 10.4 GB | 3.5 GB |
| 8 + 8, then the two rolled again | 1.62 GB | 1.50 GB | 0.92 | 99 s | 117 s | 3.71 GB | |

- The second-level row is why a rolled pack is never rolled again: rolling two 8-rolls gives 1.50 GB, about what one 16-roll gives (1.48 GB), for 99 s and 3.7 GB more.
- A roll's validate (`index-pack --threads=2` at nice 19, the 0.87 GB 8-roll) took 93 s, 162 CPU-s, 1.37 GB maxrss. So one roll of 8 costs about 3 minutes and 290 CPU-s on the home shard, against about 75 promotions' input.
- The roll kept every object: the 4-roll's index holds the same 1,540,334 objects as its inputs, and `index-pack --verify` passes.

**B0-34's cold warm with roll-up [inference from the table and round 26's phases].** repo:131296's 61 promotions (8.64 GB) rolled at ROLL_IN_MAX 2 GiB are about 8 rolls of about 8 promotions each. The two 8-rolls measured came to 0.52 and 0.41 of their input, so about 3.5 to 4.5 GB. At 104 to 132 MB/s that reads in 27 to 43 s, inside the 39 to 54 s window. Total about 100 to 127 s at 0.52, 93 to 120 s at 0.41, against 120 s. At 16 per roll (0.42, about 3.6 GB, 28 to 35 s) it would be about 94 to 118 s, but a 16-roll's 5.7 GB RSS is past the bound above. So with ROLL_IN_MAX 2 GiB the warm reaches 120 s at the R2 rate's upper half, not reliably at its lower half. Round 23b's 1.04-times-pushes figure was a whole-network `repack -a -d`; bounded rolls do not reach it. Round 34's probe (m39, standard-2) put the R2 limit per container, not per site or bucket: a second container on the same site and packs read 52.5 MB/s beside the first's 74.8, against the first's 31.2 alone in the same bins; m39's own totals (36 to 56 MB/s) were held by standard-2's one vCPU, so they do not change this estimate, which stays on standard-4's 104 to 132 MB/s: 93 to 126 s [inference].

**Beat.**
- **A whole-network roll** (`repack -a -d`): 0.32 of the input, but 8.6 to 10.4 GB resident and 385 s or more, past a 12 GiB container beside clones.
- **A geometric roll with rolled packs re-rolled:** the second level saved 8 % of its input for 99 s and 3.7 GB (table).
- **SHARED's network-chain `Compacted`:** packs, promotions and markers live on repository chains (`Promoted`, `ChainLog::last_promoted`), and no network group exists in the code.
- **Deleting consumed packs at once:** a shard mid-rehydrate, or one behind the `Compacted`, would lose packs it is about to load.

**Evidence.** `tests/am1/results/lm1-memory.md`, round 32; `tests/fanout/rollup/{rollk,level2,validate}.sh`; `tests/fanout/raw/rollup-r32.txt`.

**Flip.** A hosted B0-34 cold warm over 120 s after the roll has run, which makes AHEAD (`FETCH_AT_ONCE`) or the `/spool` early headers the next lever; a hosted roll whose RSS is past 2 times its input, which lowers ROLL_IN_MAX; or a network chain built for GC, which would move `Compacted` there with one record for both.

**The contradiction, settled.** SHARED defined `Compacted` as a `NetworkEvent` on the network chain, and DESIGN's rehydrate read it per network. The operator chose the repository-chain form (round 32's review): DESIGN wins over SHARED, the promotions, markers, and `ChainLog::last_promoted` already live on the repository chain, and no network chain exists in the code. SHARED's "Compaction never drops an object" now says the base records it on each repository chain beside `Promoted`.

**GC's pack-set guard, per chain.** SHARED's guard refuses a push that names objects it does not send, and a `RestoredTo`, when a `Compacted` committed after the pack-set index their walk read. With one `Compacted` per repository chain, the guard holds per chain, for two reasons:
- **A roll drops no object.** Its pack is `pack-objects --stdin-packs` over exactly the consumed packs, so it holds every object they held. The 4-roll kept all 1,540,334 objects, and the produced pack is validated before `Compacted` commits. A walk that read the consumed packs finds every object again in the produced one, so a roll can never make a concurrent push's walk wrong. `decide` still refuses such a push or `RestoredTo` only for a `Compacted` on its own chain, which is the chain whose packs it walked.
- **A fork's chain rolls only its own promotions.** `decide` accepts a `Compacted` only over committed `Promoted` packs of the same chain, so one chain's roll never consumes a pack another chain's walk or promotion named.

What stays open is GC itself, which will drop objects. GC must not drop an object a consumed pack held until the produced pack is loaded on every shard of the network, because a shard still behind the `Compacted` serves from the consumed packs. The sweeper's deletion rule above already waits for every shard, but GC is not built, and the rule that ties its `Compacted` to that wait is open as G9's remainder. No roll in this entry deletes an object.

**Gate risk.** B0-34's 120 s cold warm is reached only at the upper half of the R2 rate: 93 to 127 s by the inference above, against 120 s. This entry does not claim the gate. The flip below is a hosted cold warm over 120 s after the roll has run, and the next lever then is AHEAD (`FETCH_AT_ONCE`, four stored packs at once, `fetch-ahead`) or the `/spool` early headers (G9's row, `lm1-memory` round 31).

### `sweep-quiet`: the sweeper keeps each network's home for a day, so an idle install's cron wakes no `Names` member, 2026-11-17

**Status.** Asked for by the operator (rule 4, loop writers of Durable Object rows); built on branch `sweep-quiet`, not deployed. A site-script change, so it ships only through a site day.

**Decision.** The site's `*/15` sweeper keeps each network's home site in its cursor object (`Registry` object `sweep`, table `sweep_home`), and a run reads a network's home from `Names` (`RepoOwner`, then the owner's `Placement`) only when it has none cached or the cached one is HOME_FOR_MS (24 h [guess]) old, at most HOMES_PER_RUN (64 [guess]) a run, new networks first. A failed read keeps the cached home. The homes a run read are stored before it sweeps; homes of networks no bucket holds any more are dropped; a run that read none writes no home row.

**Why.** Each run read both rows for every network in the three buckets, about 180 networks and 350 `Names` member reads per site per run. On an idle `graft-m2b` that woke the `names:*` members four times an hour, and each wrote rows for the request and the 2 s drain alarms after it: 2,614 rows in 23:05 to 23:30Z on 2026-11-16, idle, every row from `names:*` members, 487 objects, in the minutes right after the 23:15 and 23:30 runs (23:15 to 23:19 and 23:30 to 23:34). Site a's run has also ended "Too many API requests by single Worker invocation" since 20:43Z on 2026-11-16, at 255 subrequests a run on every site [measured, `durableObjectsPeriodicGroups`, Workers Logs, `workersInvocationsAdaptive`; `tests/am1/results/lm1-memory.md`, "sweep-quiet"].

**What it beat.**
- **Not waking an idle member at all:** the home is needed to pick which site sweeps a network, and the leader's answer is the only source; skipping the read means a network never swept.
- **Fixing the member's 2 s drain alarm instead:** it would cut rows per wake, but every run would still wake about 350 members and spend its subrequests on them.
- **Reading the home from the registry row's first site:** the registry row lists voters in record order, not the owner's `home`, and does not follow a `Home` move.

**Evidence.** `workers/site/src/sweep.rs`, `a_run_reads_homes_only_for_new_or_day_old_networks` and `a_failed_read_keeps_the_cached_home_and_a_run_reads_at_most_its_cap`; `tests/sweepquiet/plant.py` (7 of 7 caught, the first is main's read-every-run).

**Flip.** A hosted idle hour after the site day in which `names:*` members still write rows after a cron run with no new network; or a network swept by no site for over a day after its owner's home moved.

### `burst-receipts`: the receipt asks before it reports, and a pool shard sends back a push that needs a catch-up, 2026-11-17

**Status.** Asked for by the orchestrator after B0-32 m3fr11. Built on branch `b032-trace`, not deployed. The edge part ships on an edge deploy. The shard part is a site-script change, so it ships only through a site day.

**Decision.** Two changes:
1. **Ask before report** (`crates/lookup/src/lib.rs`, `receipt`). At each `COMMIT_RECEIPT` a `/commit` send is still open, the edge asks the same member `/outcome_by_request` (the request id, the command without its pack) within `CALL_DEADLINE`, whether or not the member is `busy`. Any 200 to the ask keeps the send open. `done`, `NotLeader` or `pending` ends it, as before. Only a member that did not answer the ask with a 200 and is not `busy` either is reported with `suspect`, and the command is sent again, about 3 s after the send instead of 2 s. `receipt-rule`'s keep-open, its `RECEIPT_OPEN` and the error-status report are unchanged.
2. **A pool shard sends back a push that needs a catch-up** (`graftyard_git::on_catch_up`, `workers/site/src/shard.rs`, `"/validate"`). A push the network's first shard forwarded (`pool=1`) never waits on the pool shard for a catch-up. That covers a pool shard holding no cursor for its disk, and a 409 `missingBase` from its container. It answers 409, and the first shard sends that one push back to the caller with `x-graft-fanout-failed`, which re-sends it with `via`, as for any failed forward. Unlike a `warming` 503, it does not mark the pool shard cold. The first shard, and a pool shard asked directly, still wait as `disk-validate` says.

**Why.** On B0-32 m3fr11 (term 2 held, 0 edge errors) [measured, `tests/am1/results/lm1-rows-m3f.md`, "m3fr11 after the run"]:
- **103 suspects.** Every one of the 103 `/suspect` reports and resends fell in the burst's first 5 s, from 13 of 95 edge isolates. At each missed deadline, the isolate's last 200 from the leader was 2.1 s old at p10, 2.5 s at p50 and 3.9 s at most, never within `COMMIT_RECEIPT`. So `busy` was false, and the rule reported without asking. Leader `/commit` handlers that started at 04:31:43 to :45 ran p50 3.1 s and up to 4.6 s (353 of 521 over 2 s), against a 1 s `COMMIT_HOLD`. Meanwhile the leader's `/outcome_by_request` answered at p90 608 ms and at most 625 ms. The leader was slow to answer held commits, not gone.
- **What the misses cost.** Pushes with a miss committed in p50 5.1 s, the same as those without (5.1 s). The resends did not make commits slower. They added a 256 KiB re-send each and 103 `suspect` waves to the followers.
- **The validate p99 is ten pushes.** 489 of 499 acknowledged burst pushes validated in under 1.4 s, and the next value above 1.32 s is 15.6 s. On site a, 9 burst pushes forwarded to `pool:4` and 1 to `pool:2` waited out the edge's 15 s (`wait=15`) on their pool shard. Each pool shard was then in a catch-up of the burst's own packs, of 37 to 495 packs and 4.4 to 21 s. The wait is for the run after that one (`wait_from`). Each answered 503 `warming` at 15.2 to 15.7 s, and the first shard then validated each with `via=0` in 131 to 244 ms. The first shard's own burst validates ended within 1.1 s, except one at 6.4 s.

**What it beat.**
- **Treating any 200 in the term as `busy`:** under the burst an isolate's last 200 was up to 3.9 s old, so this needs a longer window. A longer window also spares a member that answered once and then died, until the window runs out. The ask checks the member at the moment of the miss.
- **A longer `COMMIT_RECEIPT`:** it delays the report for a member that is really gone, on every commit.
- **Shortening the leader's held `/commit`:** the 2 to 4.6 s handler is the leader's queue at the burst (`queue:slot` p99 4.5 s), which is LM-1's and B0-02's leader-side work, not the receipt's.
- **A pool shard waiting only for the entry that carries its base:** it needs the base's index, which the container does not report, and the first shard already validates these in under 250 ms.
- **Marking a pool shard cold on a missing base:** it would send every push to the first shard for 30 s over one push's base.

**Evidence.**
- `crates/lookup/src/lib.rs`, `a_slow_200_from_a_busy_member_is_the_reply_with_no_resend_or_report`: the m3fr11 case, not `busy` and answering the ask, which fails on main. Also `a_member_that_never_answered_is_still_reported`: no 200 to the ask, or a 503 to it, is reported at 2.3 s.
- `crates/git/tests/disk_validate.rs`, `a_pool_shard_sends_a_push_that_needs_a_catch_up_back`.
- `tests/m0carried/plant30.py`: 6 of 6 caught. The first is main's report-without-asking, and the fifth is main's pool-shard wait.

**Flip.**
- For the ask: a hosted run where a dead member's report comes 1 s later and that delay moves a gate line.
- For the send-back: one where pushes sent back from a pool shard put the first shard's validate p99 over the pool shard's wait.

### `sweep-wall`: a sweep run asks a failed chain once and stops starting work at 8 minutes, 2026-11-17

**Status.** Asked for by the operator (site a's 620 s sweep wall); built on branch `sweep-wall`, not deployed. A site-script change, so it ships only through a site day.

**Decision.** One `sweep_all` run asks each chain's `request` table through a run-scoped source: once a chain's lookup fails, the run answers its other packs as failed lookups without asking (kept and alarmed, `LookupFailed`), and once SWEEP_WALL (8 minutes [guess]) of the run's own clock has passed, the run asks no chain and starts no network, returns with the next network as its cursor, and its caller stores the cursor and runs the fold audit. The report gains `dead` (the chains asked once) and `walled`.

**Why.** Site a's run is serial over its networks, and `lookup::call` spends LOOKUP_FOR (20 s) on a chain no member answers. The retired B0-33 groups `repo:131322` and `repo:131323` keep their packs in the buckets after `/retire`, and every member answers 409 "member not joined": the 06:00Z run on 2026-11-17 made 3,980 member reads that answered 409 and 3,384 registry-row reads for those two chains, at a steady 270 to 370 a minute, and was cancelled at 899.5 s, the Cron Trigger's 15 minutes, as was the 06:15Z run. A cancelled run stores no cursor, so every later run starts at the same network and dies there: the 05:30 (352 s) and 05:45 (620 s) walls were the same sweep reaching those groups. The 620 s run itself spent about 270 s on network 131296's fills (979 MB of GETs) and the rest on lookup bursts of 1 to 119 s per group, 28 member objects in all [measured, Workers Logs by trace id, `r2OperationsAdaptiveGroups`; `tests/am1/results/lm1-memory.md`, "Site a's sweep wall"].

**What it beat.**
- **Concurrent networks:** cuts the wall when every group answers but not when one does not: the dead chain's thousands of lookups would still each wait LOOKUP_FOR, 16 at a time.
- **A shorter lookup for the sweeper:** a 2 s bound would cut each lookup tenfold, still minutes for a chain of 9,216 packs (131323's alarm count on 11-16), and would mark a slow live leader unavailable.
- **Storing the cursor after each network:** makes progress past the wedge, but a run still burns its whole 15 minutes on a dead chain, and the fold audit after it never runs.
- **Skipping networks whose chain has no group:** needs a probe the sweep does not have, and a retired group's packs are exactly what the sweeper must keep and alarm, not decide on.

**Evidence.** `crates/git/src/sweep.rs`, `a_chain_whose_lookup_failed_is_asked_once_a_run` and `a_run_stops_starting_networks_at_its_wall`; `tests/sweepwall/plant.py` (8 of 8 caught, the first is main's ask-every-pack with no wall).

**Flip.** A hosted run in which site a's sweep still passes SWEEP_WALL plus the in-flight network's actions, or in which a chain answered after a failed lookup in the same run held a pack the run should have marked (a committed pack left without its marker for more than one full pass).

### `read-beat`: a read round to a voter with AppendEntries out carries no entries, 2026-11-17

**Status.** Asked for by the operator (trace B0-29's commit regression, code-only). Built on branch `read-beat`, not deployed. A `crates/raft` change, so it reaches every member release on a site day.

**Decision.** `Member::read_round` sends each voter that has AppendEntries out (a non-empty pipeline and an outstanding call sent under READ_RESEND, 500 ms [guess], ago), and whose acknowledged index is in the in-memory window, an AppendEntries with no entries at that acknowledged index (`read_beat`). It leaves the pipeline and the outstanding call alone. Every other voter gets the round as before, a forced send from `next`, so a call outstanding READ_RESEND or longer is re-sent by the next round, not left to CALL_DEADLINE's tick.

**Why.** B0-29's commit p99 went from 774 ms (m27, main `2b1938e`) to 1,682 ms (`mwkyk9zg`, main `19b5ae77`), because the leader cut 3.8 entries a second against 4.8 and every command waited longer for the one entry in flight (`queue:slot` p99 462 to 4,308 ms). The leader's trace shows each entry sent 6.35 times to one voter and 7.81 times to the other. 84 to 87% of its AppendEntries to voters were repeats of the entry in flight, 639 and 936 MB against 111 and 113 MB of first sends, at the 20 to 30 ms cadence of read rounds. The followers took 29 to 31 calls a second against m27's 3 [measured, `tests/m0/results/read-beat.md`]. A forced send drops the pipeline and sends from `next`, which moves only on an ack, so every round carried the entry again. Rounds became that frequent with `lease-clock`: a leader whose stamp lag window is 250 ms or more grants no lease read, and the replayed rule had this leader suspect for 86.7% of arrivals [inference: the run saved no `/stats.clock`].

**Why READ_RESEND.** The forced rounds also re-sent a lost call within one round. With empty rounds only, the long sweep's live half failed on seed 13441: a half-hung site lost the leader's calls, nothing re-sent them until CALL_DEADLINE, the leader handed off, and a quorum with requests waiting stalled 31,166 ms against the 30 s bound; main stalls 5,273 ms on that seed. Across 12,000 live seeds the two rules' stall distributions otherwise match (p99 16.0 s both) [measured, `tests/m0/results/read-beat.md`, "The long sweep"]. With READ_RESEND the seed stalls 3,025 ms. On `mwkyk9zg` 1% and 4% of entries waited 500 ms or more for a voter's first ack, so the resend costs about one extra send for those [measured, the same trace].

**What it beat.**
- **Lease reads while the clock is suspect:** reopens the stale-read window `lease-clock` closed.
- **A longer READ_ROUND_GAP:** every read waits longer, and each round still re-sends the entry.
- **Rounds only to voters with nothing out:** a read arriving while an entry is in flight would wait for that entry's ack.
- **Empty rounds with no resend:** failed the live bound once in the long sweep, as above.

**Evidence.** `a_read_round_behind_an_entry_in_flight_resends_no_entries` (`crates/raft/tests/scenarios.rs`) fails on main `fbe49d59` ("20 of 20 read rounds re-sent the entry in flight") and passes. `a_read_round_to_a_voter_with_no_calls_out_still_carries_the_entry` and `a_read_round_resends_a_call_outstanding_past_read_resend` cover the fallbacks. `tests/m0carried/plant34.py`: 6 of 6 caught. The long sweep and Porcupine results are in `tests/m0/results/read-beat.md`.

**Flip.** A hosted B0-29 on this change in which the leader still sends a voter more than about 1.5 AppendEntries carrying entries per entry, or one in which a read was granted without a voter quorum's ack of a round sent after it arrived.

### `learner-hold`: a learner's held call ends once its answer has left in any response (F85), 2026-11-17

**Status.** Asked for by the operator after `read-beat`. Built on branch `f85-hold`, not deployed. A site-script change, so it ships only through a site day.

**Decision.** A leader remembers, per learner, the newest LEFT_KEPT (64 [guess]) read-index batches whose `ReadIndexRes` left in a response to that learner, recorded when a call's response takes what was held and from each call's own reply. A learner's call held for its batch (`READ_INDEX_HOLD`) ends once that batch is answered in its own reply, held for the learner, or remembered as sent, and each record wakes the learner's waiting calls (`workers/site/src/callers.rs`, `Callers::left` and `Callers::answered`).

**Why.** Before this, a held call ended only for an answer in its own reply or still held. On B0-29 `mwkyk9zg`, 29,660 of 92,092 learner calls into the leader left 499 ms or more after entry, and in 29,547 of them the batch had been answered before the call arrived: HEDGE copies and re-asks of answered batches, each sitting the full hold, beside 18,619 learner hedges [measured, `tests/m0/results/learner-hold.md`].

**What it beat.**
- **A shorter READ_INDEX_HOLD:** the copies would still wait, and a far learner's real round could miss it.
- **No hold:** answers would trail a learner's reads by a call again, as before B0-18's fix.
- **A longer HEDGE:** fewer copies, but each still waits 500 ms.

**Evidence.** `callers::tests::a_held_call_ends_when_its_answer_leaves_in_another_call` fails on main and passes; `tests/m0carried/plant36.py` 5 of 5 caught; B0-18's depth test passes unchanged.

**Flip.** A hosted run on this change in which learner calls held 500 ms stay above about 1% of learner calls, or learner hedges do not fall, or a learner read waits for an answer this rule let its call drop.

### `colo-unknown`: a `suspect` report from no data center counts toward no colo, 2026-11-17

**Status.** Asked for by the operator (root-cause m43's 11 `CommitErrors` step-downs); built on branch `commit-errors`, not deployed. A `crates/raft` change, so the next site day ships it.

**Decision.** `Colo(0)` is `Colo::UNKNOWN`. A follower counting `suspect` reports toward `SUSPECT`'s two colos skips a report from `Colo::UNKNOWN`; the report still answers its verdict, marks a stall, and starts a campaign once the promise has lapsed. Every edge request sets its colo from `cf.colo`; a site script never calls `set_colo`, so its lookups (shard, audit, prsync, broker, merge queue) report with colo 0.

**Why.** On B0-33 m43 every edge request came from LAX (2,961 of 2,961 edge log events sampled in the load carried `cf.colo` LAX). The 11 `CommitErrors` step-downs were holds (`to: None`): none moved a leader. The 19 term changes came from elections, each after both followers stopped renewing their promises while the leader kept appending and committing (in the 10 s before each lapse, 2 to 43 appends reached each follower and its commit rose by 1 to 17), and once the promises lapsed the next report started a campaign. A follower stops renewing for one of three reasons: an append carrying a transfer, `sent_at < transfer_at`, or `suspect` withholding. A transfer lasts at most LEASE (9 s): it completes in a new term or is abandoned, and the next append renews. Yet in 21 of 28 lapses an append of the same term reached the follower more than 9 s after its last renewal and still renewed nothing, and no StepDown alarm named a target. That leaves withholding, which needs two distinct colos inside 10 s, and with one edge colo the only second colo is 0: 15 site-script isolates sent 667 `/suspect` reports and 49 read-only isolates 1,321, beside 143,954 from 315 edge commit isolates. Replaying the `SUSPECT` rule on each follower's own trace with colo 0 for the site-script and read-only isolates (the trace cannot tell a read-only edge isolate from a site script's) puts the last renewal inside the window the promise samples bound in 8 of 28 lapses, and with one colo for everything in 0 of 28: without colo 0 no follower would have withheld at all. The match is partial because members do not log a report's colo; `Trace::Reported` (28) now does [measured, `tests/am1/results/lm1-memory.md`, "m43's CommitErrors step-downs"].

**The CommitErrors trips themselves.** Legitimate by the rule as written, and harmless: every miss was a deadline miss to a live follower whose handler ran in p50 0 ms but whose input queue held 900 to 3,800 requests ahead of the call, nearly all edge `/read` and `/suspect`; a hold changes no leader. They are the load's symptom, the same class as F74, and stay out of this change.

**What it beat.**
- **Site scripts set their site's colo:** a site is not an edge data center, and three site ids would let site scripts on two sites withhold from a healthy leader by themselves.
- **Excusing queue-delayed misses in `health.rs`:** the trips were holds that moved nothing, so it would not have removed one term change.
- **Per-member `/suspect` damping:** fewer reports from the same two colos still withhold.

**Evidence.** `an_unknown_colo_is_no_second_witness_but_still_starts_a_campaign` (`crates/raft/tests/leadership.rs`) fails on main (B withheld on LAX plus colo-0 reports) and passes; `tests/colounknown/plant.py` plants main's rule, a skip that clears the window, an `UNKNOWN` other than the 0 a site script sends, and an early return that drops the campaign: 4 of 4 caught. The simulator's colos now start at 1 so its clients are edges. Long sweep (2,000 seeds, live half 4,000) passed, longest stretches 16.3, 27.9 and 25.4 s; Porcupine Ok on all three histories.

**Flip.** A gray leader that only site-script reports could have moved, or a hosted run where both followers still withhold with one edge colo (read `Trace::Reported`).

### `read-ahead`: a leader holds up to READ_AHEAD frozen batches when a dependency read outlasts a round, 2026-11-17

**Status.** Asked for by the orchestrator after B0-31's buckets-up trace. Built on branch `read-ahead`, not deployed. A `crates/raft` change, so it reaches every member release on a site day.

**Decision.**
- **Batches.** The leader holds up to `read_ahead(round, read)` = ceil(mean read / mean round) frozen batches behind the entry in flight, at least 1 and at most READ_AHEAD (3 [guess]). The old single held batch is `read_ahead` 1, which is still the case while a read fits in a round (`crates/raft/src/member/leader.rs`, `cut_early`, `Lead::deciding` as a queue).
- **Timing.** With `held` batches frozen, the next is cut, and its reads are asked, `held + 1` mean rounds after the entry in flight was appended, less one mean read. So each batch's read lands about when the entry before it commits.
- **Deciding.** Batches are decided oldest first, each only once the entry before it committed and applied, on the fold then, with exactly the chains `deps()` names on that fold. A chain the earlier entry newly named is read again for that batch alone. A read it no longer names is dropped.
- **Unchanged.** A read's answer goes to the batch whose `DepsWanted` id it carries. A transfer drops every held batch's reads, a leadership end answers every held batch `NotLeader`, and a reconfiguration waits until none is held.

**Why.** B0-31's apac leader read its owner's identity groups on enam at `deps:all` p50 368 ms (Authz 293 ms), against a round of p50 198 ms. With one batch held, the cycle is the read plus `decide`, not the round: 726 entries in 300 s, one per 413 ms. `queue:slot` was p50 531 ms and p99 1,701 ms, and commit p99 1,439 ms against the 1 s line. Across six B0-31 runs that held their leader, commit p99 followed `deps:all` (1,118 ms at 356 ms up to 2,138 ms at 485 ms), and rounds stayed between 194 and 254 ms [measured, `tests/am1/results/lm1-rows-m3f.md`, "B0-31's buckets-up commit tail"].

**The invariants, against AGENTS.md:**
1. **`decide` is pure on the fold, the entry's earlier commands, and reads asked after its commands were admitted.**
   - Each batch's commands are cut from admission before its own `DepsWanted` is asked, as before. A later batch only holds commands admitted after the earlier cut.
   - A batch is decided only by `decide_held` on the front of the queue. That runs only with no entry in flight, so `applied` is the log's end.
   - It decides with exactly the chains `deps()` names on that fold.
2. **A follower verifies k+1 only after it applies k.** Nothing about a held batch reaches a follower: the leader appends one entry at a time, only after the one in flight committed. The followers see the same log as before, one entry after another.
3. **No read made for batch k+2 is used after entry k+1 changed what it depends on.**
   - A read is keyed to one chain. `decide_held` keeps only the reads of the chains the fold names after k+1 applied.
   - If k+1 moved a command's dependency (a transfer's new owner, a settings change), the early read of the old chain is dropped, and the new chain is read then, for that batch only.
   - If k+1 changed the dependency's own content instead, such as an Authz revocation committed on the Authz chain, that is not this group's entry. The read binds as it always did: a revocation acknowledged before the read binds it, and one acknowledged after binds the next entry's. This is the same rule as one held batch, since the read was still asked after the batch's commands were admitted.

**What it beat.**
- **Reading dependency folds once and caching them across entries:** "read once per entry through `fresh`" forbids it. It would break BF-2, BF-15 and BF-27.
- **Deciding a held batch on the fold before the entry ahead of it applied:** this breaks "one entry in flight". Planted (`plant32.py` 6), it fails 9 of the 11 `deps.rs` tests.
- **Moving the identity groups' leaders with the repository:** the orchestrator ruled no placement change. Identity groups follow the owner's record by design (OPEN-QUESTIONS F81).

**Evidence.**
- `crates/raft/tests/deps.rs`:
  - `reads_longer_than_a_round_overlap_two_batches_so_the_cycle_is_about_a_round`: with a 200 ms round and 370 ms reads, one entry per 380 ms on main and per 200 ms here, never two in flight.
  - `a_failed_or_stale_read_for_a_later_batch_leaves_the_earlier_batch_alone`: a missing, failed or stale read for k+2 leaves k+1 deciding as it would alone. k+2 re-reads the chain k+1 named, so a revocation in the stale read binds nothing.
  - `the_re_read_goes_to_the_batch_being_decided`.
  - `a_transfer_drops_every_held_batchs_deps`.
- `tests/m0carried/plant32.py`: 7 of 7 caught. The first plant is main's single batch.
- The 2,000-seed simulator sweep, whose dependency reads answer 0 to 400 ms late, checks one entry in flight per leader and that every command an entry decided was admitted before its reads were asked. It passed: 2,000 seeds in each half, 6,694 early asks and 585 re-reads in the harsh half, and Porcupine found the histories linearizable (153,324 harsh, 2,246,911 gray and 5,971,926 live operations). The full checks passed with 1,099 tests and 0 failed.
- The latency gain on Cloudflare is unmeasured. The next B0-31 decides it.

**Flip.**
- A hosted B0-31 where the cycle stays read-bound with two batches held.
- Or a simulator or hosted case where a held batch's command was decided on a read asked before it was admitted.

### A running install keeps its snapshots for its life (G21, 2026-11-17)

**Decision.** (i-2) is replaced (`design/DESIGN.md`, Shape, `CHILD_GROUP_AT`, Installs; `crate::load::next_job`, `crate::load::retry_batch`):
- A running install's snapshot keys are pinned. A newer source extends the job to its `through` with the archives past the job's own end, whatever snapshots it names and whichever leader sent it, when those archives continue the job's. The job then answers the newer round.
- A source from the same leader (same `from`, term and boot) with an earlier `through` than the job's is a late delivery: it is dropped, and `load_want` keeps the job's round.
- A job starts again only when no install runs, when the newer archives leave a gap after the job's end (or reach `through` with none), or when a source from another leader or term names an earlier `through`, whose round the job could not answer. Each restart logs its reason.
- A batch that fails (a network error reading R2, the database full) keeps the job and is tried again `RETRY_MS` later. The job is abandoned on the `BATCH_TRIES`th failure in a row, as a batch that kills its isolate already is. An audit's failure ends it at once, as before.

**Why.** On B0-30's short runs the install never finished under load (G21). In b030r5, site c's install restarted at each leader snapshot, 22 times from 07:06 to 07:36Z, because each new core snapshot changed the source's keys and (i-2) restarted on any key change. Its applied stayed at 4,968, and its member wrote 4.03M rows in 18 minutes. A burst of 39 restarts at 06:54:48Z came from deliveries queued while the member dropped its tables: their `through` went 5,607, 5,623, 5,603, so each late one restarted the job. One "Network connection lost" at 07:57:38Z threw away a 9-minute load with no load running (`tests/am1/results/b030-split.md`, "Phases (b030r5)") [measured]. The job's own snapshots plus the archives after them reach any later `through` with the same fold as the newer snapshot does, since the fold is deterministic, so a new key is never a reason to start again.

**Pin by retention [doc in code].** `snap::retain` deletes only snapshots whose rows `snapshots_to_keep` dropped, and that keeps every snapshot inside `RESTORE_WINDOW` (35 days by entry time) plus the newest before it. No path deletes an archive object. So the leader keeps the pinned snapshots far past any install without a lease or a pin record. A pinned object that is gone anyway fails the batch, which the retry rule abandons after `BATCH_TRIES`, and the next source starts a job from the current snapshots.

**Beat.**
- A minimum spacing between restarts: each restart still throws away the load, so under steady snapshots a 30-minute spacing gives a 30-minute window to finish a load that takes an hour, and the install still never ends.
- Restarting only once the source is gone: the source changes on every truncation, and the old one is never gone within an install, so it equals the pin, but stated on objects instead of keys.
- A leader that pins its source while a follower installs: a `crates/raft` change for what retention already gives.
- (i-1)'s wish that an install move to the slimmed metadata snapshot when it commits: the amended (i-3) drops the member's own metadata first, so the pre-slim load peaks at about 7.7 GB [inference], under `CHILD_GROUP_AT`. Moving to it would restart the load for each new metadata snapshot, every 256 MB of log after the slim pass ends.

**Evidence.** `a_newer_snapshot_mid_install_extends_the_pinned_job` and `a_late_source_from_the_same_leader_changes_nothing` fail on main, which restarts on both. `only_a_gap_or_another_leaders_earlier_source_restarts` and `a_failed_install_batch_is_retried_before_it_is_abandoned` (`workers/site/src/load.rs`). Plants in `tests/b030fixes/plant.py`.
