This leaves C20's send question open.

**Beat.** The KV path with `allowUnconfirmed` and an explicit `sync()` before every reply.

**Evidence.** `tests/am1/results/c-design.md`, "What holds the leader's sends" and "(c1b) under review" [measured]; `tests/fanout/votershed/p3*.py`, `p4*.py`.

**Flip.** A run where the leader's open requests are held under a bound, by a cap on held commit waiters or any other means, and the output gate's share of the round-trip excess is still over 30%.

### F88: a committed entry folds by its own format, and a golden-digest corpus pins every kind, 2026-11-18

**Status.** Built on branch `f88-format-fold`, the operator's option (a) through the orchestrator (T-01a17bda), from this thread's trace (T-01a1d805, `decisions/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`, F88). Lands before the next site day on any install.

**Decision.** `Tiered::write` takes the entry's `format` (`crates/fold/src/tier.rs`), and `RepoEvent::Promoted` writes its `promoted_log` row only in a 32.25 entry (`REPO_FORMAT_ROLLUP`, `crates/git/src/tiers.rs`). The archive step records a promotion in 32.25 only once `GRAFTYARD_ROLLUP` is on, and in 32.1 otherwise (`crates/git/src/log_archive.rs`), so a 32.1 promotion folds as it did before roll-up on every release and no roll can consume it. A scratch view writes at the newest format (`SCRATCH_FORMAT`): only `check_compacted` reads `promoted_log` there, against a fold that logged only 32.25 promotions. `crates/git/tests/fold_corpus.rs` folds one fixture per `RepoEvent` kind (`fold_corpus.json`) at every format version it can be committed at, 902 rows, against `fold_corpus.golden`: versions 1 to 24 pinned on main `0d212879`, the release before roll-up, and version 25 on `e2bddc92`, roll-up's merge. A digest that moves fails and names the kind and version.

**Why.** Roll-up changed what an existing 32.1 event writes, in place. Members that applied their promotions live before the upgrade kept digests without the row, and the fold audit's refold on the new release added it, so every audited chain with a promotion in its tail alarmed (F88; 26 of 26 alarming audits on `graft-m3f`). A committed entry must fold the same on every release, so an event's fold depends on its format, not on the running release (`design/SHARED.md`, "Schema change is a refold, never a migration"). Nothing caught it: `wire_tags.golden` pins encodings, not what an event writes.

**What it beat.**
- **(b) A dedicated release that reads both schemas and refolds lazily.** It is the design's rule for a real install, but no product install holds data, and it costs a release cycle for one table.
- **(c) A committed backfill event for `promoted_log`.** It needs a new event and a leader step per chain, for rows only roll-up reads.
- **Pinning only the reproduction test.** It catches this event and no other; the corpus covers every kind at every format.

**Test-only cleanup is not precedent.** Chains whose members applied 32.1 promotions on the roll-up release (2026-11-16 18:29Z on) hold `promoted_log` rows that this release's refold will not write, so their audits alarm once more. They are all on test installs, which are reseeded or retired by their owners (`tests/am1/results/lm1-rows-m3f.md`, "F88 fixed: a committed entry folds by its own format"), not backfilled. On an install that holds real data, a change to what a committed event writes ships only in SHARED's dual-read release.

**Evidence.** `crates/git/tests/encoding.rs`, `a_committed_promoted_entry_folds_to_the_digest_it_had_when_it_committed`: core digest `4ceb4070…77cc`, as on `0d212879`; it fails on main (`d5c31b8e…d51f`). `crates/git/tests/rollup.rs`, `a_promotion_committed_before_roll_up_is_not_rollable`; `crates/git/tests/log_archive.rs`, `a_promotion_takes_the_roll_up_format_only_when_roll_up_is_on`. `fold_corpus` on `e2bddc92` differs from `0d212879` in exactly `Promoted` 1 to 24, and on this branch matches both. `tests/m0carried/plant40.py`: 4 of 4 caught, including roll-up's unconditional write (`Promoted 1` to `24` named).

**Flip.** A kind whose fold must change for an existing format, which then needs the dual-read release and a cited edit of its corpus rows; or a corpus that misses a planted fold change, which means the fixtures need more setup state.

### `merge-tail`: a leader that answered is cached without a config, and the edge's shard reads carry the record, 2026-11-18

Branch `merge-tail` (`tests/m0/results/merge-tail.md`), from B0-29 run 5's merge p99 (12,516 ms) and push resolve p99
(6,039 ms). Built in this thread (T-01a1ccdd) on the orchestrator's ask (T-01a17bda).

**Decision.** `graftyard_lookup`'s cache keeps the member that last answered as leader (`Known::answered`), and
`cached_leader` returns it when the config held names no leader on that site, or no config is held. A reply naming a
leader on another site drops it. The edge's `shard_read` sends the owner's placement record (`record=`), as
`/validate` and `/merge` already did.

**Why.** An isolate learned a chain's voters only from a `NotLeader`, and `cached_leader` needed the leader among them.
A system chain whose leader always answers (`names:708`, `names:152` on graft-m2b) never sends one, so every read of
it went through the lookup's mark (`lookup-poll`), one request per isolate at a time: in a 6 s sample of site a, 2,718
of 4,203 member `/read`s were walk posts, one isolate's 120 posts to the same leader never overlapped, and slow merges
spent 76% of their wall with no Durable Object call running [measured]. Separately, every upload-pack on the shard
read `RepoOwner` and `Placement` because `shard_read` sent no record, and 1,869 of them threw after LOOKUP_FOR on
`names:708` [measured]; the shard's 32 lost answers fell next to those exceptions [measured] (how one invocation's
exception loses another's answer is [unverified]).

**What it beat.** Learning the config by a `/status` read on the first answer (`learn_voters`): a second call per
chain per isolate, and the config is not needed to post the member that just answered. Sharing the lookup on system
chains without a mark: `lookup-poll`'s evidence (558 to 577 posts without it in `tests/lookupbed`) still holds for a
chain with no leader. Caching `resolve` for writes: a write's fresh read is the design's rule (`rcache`).

**Evidence.** `tests/m0/results/merge-tail.md`, section 1. Test `a_leader_found_by_its_bootstrap_name_is_cached`
(`crates/lookup`); `tests/m0carried/plant41.py` 6 of 6.

**Flip.** A hosted run in which the walk posts stay a large share of member `/read`s with this build, or in which a
cached answered member serves a read after its group moved its leader (the next post would miss once and walk, as a
cached voter does today).

### M4-WP3 slice A: the launch service, 2026-11-18

**Status.** Approved by the lead (T-01a17bda) as slice A of the rest of M4-WP3, code-only. Built on branch `launch-svc` from main `dcef0f59`. It changes the job message (a site day, since `acquirejob` builds it on the shard leader) and adds an edge route (an edge day). Neither is run for it alone.

**Decision.**
- **The endpoint.** `runsvc::job_message` sets `system.github.launch_endpoint` to the install's root (`Urls::launch`). The runner creates its launch client only when that variable is set and `SystemVssConnection` has an access token (`Runner.Worker/JobRunner.cs:72-82`). It posts to `new Uri(endpoint, "/actions/build/{plan}/jobs/{job}/runnerresolve/actions")`, an absolute path, so any path in the endpoint is dropped (`Sdk/WebApi/WebApi/LaunchHttpClient.cs:42`).
- **The route.** The edge takes that path only for a `POST` whose bearer token is the run service's job token for the job the path names (`launch::job_of_path`), before any other route. Every other request routes as before, so no existing reply changes: the path is not under `/api/v3`, `/_services/` or a GHES route, and without the job's token it falls through to whatever answered it before. That includes a repository named `actions/build`, whose git and web paths a runner's job token never reaches.
- **Resolution, on the install only.** Each `{"action": "owner/repo", "version"}` (`LaunchContracts.cs:8-27`) resolves `owner/repo` through the edge's own lookup (`api::read_as`, case-insensitive as every repository route, renames followed) as an anonymous caller. Its version resolves as a full 40-hex SHA in either case, which must be a commit the network's git cache holds (`commit_object`, as REST's `commits/{sha}`), else as a full ref, a tag, then a branch, git's order (`launch::resolve`). The refs come from the narrow `tarball` read, whose rows `graftyard_api::release::resolve` records in the same order. There is no fallback to github.com or any other host, and no Cloudflare API call.
- **The reply.** 200 `{"actions": {"<action>@<version>": {name, resolved_name, resolved_sha, tar_url, zip_url, version}}}`, keyed by the request's own text, because the runner looks each action up by `"{Name}@{Ref}"` with an ordinal comparer (`ActionManager.cs:1589-1617`). If any action fails to resolve, the whole call is 422 `{"errors": {"<key>": {"message"}}}`, the shape `ActionDownloadResolutionErrorCollection` reads and joins with ". " (`LaunchHttpClient.cs:52-66`, `LaunchContracts.cs:89-106`). The messages follow GitHub's: "repository not found", "unable to find version", and the abbreviated-SHA refusal. A read that failed is a 503 instead, which the runner retries.
- **Abbreviated SHAs.** 4 to 39 hex characters that name no ref are refused with a 422, as GitHub does [doc: "Using pre-written building blocks in your workflow", full-length commit SHA]. A tag whose name is hex still resolves as that tag.
- **The 422 flag.** The job message also sets `actions_display_helpful_actions_download_errors` to `true`. Only under it does the runner read a 422's messages and not retry (`Runner.Common/Constants.cs:172`, `ActionManager.cs:1067`, `Runner.Common/LaunchServer.cs:49-54`). Without it, runner 2.338.2 parsed the 422 body as a reply and failed the job with "Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'Actions')" [measured].
- **The archive.** `tar_url` and `zip_url` are the install's codeload URLs for the resolved SHA, `{codeload}/legacy.tar.gz/{sha}`, which the edge serves itself with no redirect (`api::codeload`). Its archive has one top directory, which the runner unwraps (`ActionManager.cs:1366-1374`). The reply carries no `authentication`, so the runner sends the job's `github.token` (`ActionManager.cs:1117-1128`). That token is empty until slice B, so an anonymous read is the only one that works, which is why resolution reads anonymously too.

**What it beat.**
- **`tar_url` at the API's `/repos/{o}/{r}/tarball/{sha}`.** That answers a 302 to codeload, which the runner's `HttpClient` follows, but it adds a round trip and a second route that must keep the job's credential.
- **Reading the action repository as the job's repository.** That would let a job reach any private repository its owner's members can read before there is an access setting that says which. It waits for F90.
- **Resolving through the run service on the shard leader.** That adds a hop through the lookup to a member that holds none of the action repository's rows.

**Evidence.** Runner 2.338.2, unmodified, under `crates/actions/examples/runsvc_host.rs`, which serves the same `launch` module over two local mirror repositories (`tests/m4/results/m4-wp3-launch.md`). On main `c2b7eac4` `tests/m4/wp3/run/uses.yml` failed with "Launch client is not initialized" after 3 attempts. On this branch it succeeded: `Mirror/Hello@v1`, `mirror/hello@main` and the full SHA each downloaded and ran. `tests/m4/wp3/run/uses-refused.yml`'s five jobs each failed at once, with one 422 and no retry: an abbreviated SHA, a private repository, `actions/checkout@v4` (not on the install), a full SHA the repository lacks, and a missing tag. Kept tests: `runsvc::tests::a_job_message_names_the_launch_endpoint_and_asks_for_its_errors` fails on main; `launch::tests` cover resolution order, the reply keys and shapes, and the job-token check. Plants 48 to 57 in `tests/m4/wp3/plant.py`.

**Flip.** A runner release that resolves actions some other way, or that needs fields in the reply that this one leaves out (`package_details` for immutable actions); or a GHES reply shape this one fails to match, found against a real GHES.

### G26: the git cache shard's HEAD is the default branch, 2026-11-18

**Status.** Built on branch `g26-head` from main `3e548e95`, as the orchestrator (T-01a17bda) asked after B0-34's combined run. Container, git crate and site script; it ships on a site day with the git image.

**Decision.** The shard names HEAD as the repository's `default_branch`, as the edge's v2 ls-refs already does. The member's `ranges` read, which every catch-up already makes for `ChainLog::head`, also answers the `settings` row's `default_branch` (null before the first `Settings`). A rehydrate passes it as `&head=` on its last `PUT /refs` page. A catch-up passes it with a `POST /refs` only when it differs from the one the disk's `IngestCursor` recorded, because a `Settings` entry that changes the default carries no ref change. The container points HEAD at it whether or not the branch exists yet, so an unset default is an unborn HEAD, as GHES answers. A `head` that is not under `refs/heads/` is refused 400. With no changes, that `POST` takes no network lock: HEAD is one reftable write under git's own lock. Without `head` (an older shard object, or a member that answers none), a PUT keeps the old rule, `refs/heads/main` if it exists, else the page's first ref, so the image and the site script may ship in either order.

**Why.** G26 (`decisions/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`): for a repository whose default branch is not `main`, or has none, the shard's v0 advertisement and every v2 ls-refs the edge still forwards (`peel` over tags, a partial page, an unborn HEAD, a failed read) named a HEAD GHES would not, so a client that does not opt in would clone another branch. GHES documents the default branch as the branch a clone checks out [doc, https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@3.22/pull-requests/reference/branches], and github.com's recorded answers name it where `main` also exists (`crates/git/tests/ls_refs/axios-source.ans`) [measured].

**What it beat.**
- **A HEAD field on every `LogPacks`.** A `Settings` entry would have to name the default in each entry's JSON, and a rehydrate would still need it from somewhere for the refs pages. The `ranges` read already runs on every catch-up and reads the fold.
- **Naming HEAD on every catch-up.** It costs one `/refs` call per catch-up, about 10 a minute on a hot network, for a value that changes perhaps once in a repository's life.
- **Keeping main-or-first when the default branch does not exist yet.** GHES answers an unborn HEAD then, and a later push of that branch must not need a rehydrate to fix HEAD.

**Evidence.** `TestRefsHeadIsTheDefaultBranch` (`containers/git/server/refs_test.go`): with `dev` the default and `main` present, HEAD, the v2 ls-refs' `symref-target` and the v0 advertisement's `symref=HEAD:` all name `dev`; an empty `POST` (a catch-up over a `Settings` entry) moves HEAD to `main` and one with changes back to `dev`; an unset default (`trunk`) is `unborn HEAD symref-target:refs/heads/trunk`; a `POST` without `head` leaves HEAD and a `PUT` without it keeps the old rule; `head=HEAD` is 400. On main it fails at the first check ("HEAD refs/heads/main after a PUT naming dev"). `head_follows_the_default_branch_and_is_named_only_when_it_changes` (`crates/git/tests/catchup.rs`): a rehydrate names HEAD once, unchanged catch-ups name nothing, a changed default is named once, a new disk names it again, and an older member's answer names nothing. `the_ranges_read_answers_the_default_branch` (`workers/site/src/fanout.rs`). `tests/g26/plant.py`: nine mutants, all caught (mutant 2, an empty change set that never names HEAD, survived until the test sent the catch-up's empty `POST`).

**Flip.** A GHES 3.22 recording whose HEAD, for a repository whose default branch is not `main`, names anything but the default branch; or a hosted run where the shard's v0 or v2 HEAD differs from the edge's for the same repository.

**Amended 2026-11-19 (`b034-next`): a repository with no `Settings` row reads `refs/heads/main`.** B0-34 mt3's monorepo had no row (`b034setup.mjs`'s test-faults owner path), so `ranges` answered null, the shard sent no `head=`, and the container's main-or-first rule put HEAD on a row push's branch after each rehydrate: 15 over-the-cap misses, as in m1b34 (`tests/am1/results/b034-mt.md`). A product path leaves a live repository with no row too: a create on an edge with 32.13 enabled but not 0x12.11 and 32.17 (pre-F59) whose edge dies after `RepoOwner` has no finisher, and any create is rowless until its `InitRepo` or `Audit`'s `Lifecycle::Init` commits. Every other read already takes such a repository as `main` (`graftyard_git::transfer`, `graftyard_api::repos::defaults`). So the default lives in one place, `graftyard_git::tiers::default_branch`, which the member's `ranges` read (the shard's HEAD) and its `lsRefs` read (the edge's HEAD) both call; the edge's ls-refs now answers a rowless repository too instead of sending it to the shard. Fixing only the harness would have left the shard and the edge disagreeing on such a repository. Evidence: `the_ranges_read_answers_the_default_branch` asserts `refs/heads/main` from both reads before the first `Settings` (fails on main: `Null`); `tests/b034next/plant.py` mutants 0 to 3.

### Writes to an upload-pack's caller have a deadline, 2026-11-19

**Status.** Built on branch `b034-next` from main `81ab3b9c`. Git image; ships on a site day.

**Decision.** Each write and flush of an upload-pack answer to its caller (`flushOnWrite`, `containers/git/server/compose.go`) must complete within `clientWriteTimeout`, 30 s [guess], through `http.ResponseController.SetWriteDeadline`. A write past it fails: a stock answer's copy stops, kills `upload-pack`, and releases the network's shared lock; a spooled one goes on to its file alone (`tee`), with the lock already released.

**Why.** B0-34 mt3: from about 20:36Z one stock `pack-objects` on each of sites b and c held the monorepo's lock for 15 minutes at frozen CPU (39.28 s and 30.42 s, every `shardprocs` sample to the 20:51 sweep). Its caller had stopped reading but kept the connection open, so the write blocked rather than failed and `TestCancelledCloneReleasesTheLock`'s path never ran. No catch-up stored again on those objects (c's last at 672.9 s, b's at 596 s), and every later upload-pack there answered 503 `warming` within its deadline: 64 on c and 67 on b after 600 s. That, not a missing chain, was "site c had no compose chain": bucket c holds no `compose/` files by design, since c is not one of the network's warm sites, and c composed 30 misses before 600 s from a's and b's chains [measured, `tests/am1/results/b034-mt.md`, Workers Logs `raw/shardev-mt3.jsonl.xz`].

**What it beat.**
- **Aborting the object's fetch to the container when the edge's request goes.** The object's side is the reader that stopped; aborting it needs a signal threaded through `ShardHost::call` and covers only callers the runtime cancels. The deadline covers every caller in one place.
- **A deadline on the whole answer.** A 5 GB clone over a slow link is legitimate; a write that makes no progress for 30 s is not.

**Evidence.** `TestStalledCloneReleasesTheLock` (`containers/git/server/convoy_test.go`): a raw TCP caller reads 64 bytes of a 32 MB answer and stops, holding the connection; an `/ingest` must then finish. It fails on main after 20 s. `tests/b034next/plant.py` mutant 4.

**Flip.** A hosted row where a stock `pack-objects` stays in `shardprocs` with constant CPU for over a minute; or legitimate clones failing with write timeouts (a reading caller slower than 64 KiB in 30 s).

### `b034-tails`: one deadline per upload-pack, a stock cap, and over-the-cap misses composed after the step, 2026-11-18

**Status.** Built, trimmed, on branch `b034-tails` from main `0d64813b`. The orchestrator (T-01a17bda) approved decisions 1, 2, 3 and 5 and held 4; this entry follows the m1b34 attribution (`tests/am1/results/b034-attr.md`). Not yet measured hosted.

**Decision.**
1. **Every wait of one upload-pack shares one deadline.** These are `Compose::ready`, the running catch-up in `compose_then_catch_up` (today `Jobs::idle`, unbounded), the later catch-up, and a stock slot. The deadline is the caller's `wait`: 15 s on the edge's first site, 60 s on the others (`VALIDATE_WAIT_*`). Past it, the object answers 503 `warming` and the edge asks the next site, as a validate does. The last site's 503 reaches git as `HTTP 503`, which is what a clone sees today.
2. **Over the diff cap is retried like "not a ref tip".** A 409 `stock: over the diff cap` starts the chain's step (`Compose::start(true)`). The miss composes again after that step and the running catch-up, then after one that starts later, within the deadline. The container's step builds a base instead of a part when the chain tree differs from the new tip in more than `composeDiffMax` entries, so a chain on a wrong tip is replaced at its next step. A want still refused, `include-tag` on an annotated tag, or no chain goes to stock.
3. **Stock is admitted, not queued on the lock.** The container runs at most `stockMax` = 2 [guess] stock upload-packs, counted from start until the process ends, and answers 429 `x-graft-stock: full` at once past that; ls-refs and the advertisement take no slot. The shard object queues the rest in arrival order (`StockLine`, `STOCK_MAX` and `STOCK_POLL` in `crates/git/src/compose.rs`): only the head re-asks, every 500 ms, and a place past the deadline leaves the line and answers 503 `warming`. The client never sees the 429. The next hosted row's count of concurrent stock processes per container is what measures 2. A spooled fill holds its slot until its file is complete; a cancelled client's process is already killed (`TestCancelledCloneReleasesTheLock`).
4. **Held: stock takes no network lock.** Not built. A per-network reader count would replace the lock for stock, with `/evict` answering 409 while it is above zero and a fresh `/init` waiting for it. G26 removes what built m1b34's queue (a base on a one-file row tip, so stock on every miss after the rehydrate), and decision 3 bounds the readers to 2, so the gain is unmeasured, while it adds a reader-versus-`moveIn` exposure (below). Flip: the next row still shows a catch-up waiting over 1 s for the exclusive lock behind stock readers.
5. **`midx_ms`.** `/ingest` answers the midx write's time beside `lock_ms`, and the shard sums it in `StoredMs`.

**What a client sees.**
- **"Not a ref tip" during a catch-up:** composed once the running catch-up ends, as now. That took p50 2.8 s and p99 10.3 s in j9 (54 misses) and p50 5.7 s and p99 13.2 s in the kill phase (24). The wait is the catch-up's own length, and this change does not shorten it.
- **Past the deadline on every site:** 503.
- **Stock when the slots are full:** a wait, not an error. git retries neither 429 nor 503 unless `http.maxRetries` is set, and then only 429 [doc, git-config, `http.maxRetries`, "Set to 0 (the default) to disable retries"]. GHES documents its own Git rate limit as making "Git operations more likely to fail under high load" [doc, https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@3.22/admin/configuring-settings/configuring-user-applications-for-your-enterprise/configuring-rate-limits]. So an immediate git-shaped refusal fails the clone where a short wait would not.

**Why.**
- **m1b34's over-the-cap misses were a chain on the wrong tip.** The diff cap itself was not the cause [measured, `tests/am1/results/b034-attr.md`, "Correction"].
  - Before site a's post-kill rehydrate ended (476 s), 399 of 404 miss lines composed. Of the 193 after it, 1 did: 128 named the cap, and 95 were 503s.
  - The chain tree in the container's `diff-tree` at 10:36:46Z on site b, `75db6f44`, is in neither linux's history nor the seed plan's 854 commits.
  - Over the row's 600 real tip moves, a want differs from the tip 20 moves back by at most 2,969 entries, far under 20,000.
  - Cause [inference]: the rehydrate's refs page named `main` at a tip whose pack it had not loaded yet. `handleRefs` skipped `main` and pointed HEAD at the first ref, a row push holding one file, and the builder's `/compose?start=1` built the base there.
  - A local container test reproduces the container half: a PUT whose `main` names a missing object, with no `head=`, leaves HEAD on the first ref, and the step builds a base there. With G26's `head=refs/heads/main`, HEAD is unborn and the step builds nothing.
  - G26 (main since `g26-head`) removes this cause on the next site day. Decision 2's base-on-a-big-diff is the backstop for any other wrong tip.
- **The queue was stock readers holding the lock shared** for 20 to 99 s while a catch-up's `adopt` waited for it alone (29 to 36 s, three times). Every validate that arrived meanwhile queued behind that writer. Decision 3 bounds how many readers there are, and 4 takes them off the lock.
- **The unbounded `idle`.** 25 of the 50 shard 503s waited out a stuck catch-up before their 15 s started.

**What it beat.**
- **A 429 to the client when the slots are full.** git fails the clone at once by default.
- **A per-network cap instead of per-container.** The 2.6 GB processes share one container's 12 GiB whichever network they serve.
- **Stock keeping the lock, with only the cap.** Two 99 s readers still hold a writer, and every reader after it, for 99 s.
- **Compose over the cap from two trees.** A composed pack then carries most of both trees, which is why the cap exists.

**Risks of stock without the lock (held option 4).**
- **A repack's `-d`, or an evict, under a running stock read.** The repack already runs beside readers without the lock: git keeps open packs readable and re-reads the pack directory for one it lost ("Amended 2026-11-12 (LM-1 round 7)" above). Evict and init are covered by the reader count.
- **A midx write.** The ingest's midx write is a temp-file rename, which a reader that already mapped the old midx does not see. The repack's `--write-midx` already runs beside readers.
- **Not covered: a reader that lists the pack directory between the ingest's pack rename and idx rename.** `moveIn` renames the pack before its index, so a reader sees no index without its pack [inference: as for composed misses since round 26, which hold no lock].

**Evidence (tests, then plants that put main's rule back).**
- **Go (container), `containers/git/server/stockmax_test.go`:**
  - `TestStockFetchesPastStockMaxAreRefusedAtOnce`: with two stock fetches held open by a git wrapper, a third answers 429 `full` within 1 s, an ls-refs still reaches git, and once both end a fetch runs and no slot stays counted.
  - `TestComposeStepOnAFarChainBuildsABase`: with `composeDiffMax` 20 and a chain 40 files from HEAD, the step builds a base, not a part.
  - `TestIngestReportsTheMidxWrite`: `/ingest` answers `midx_ms` above 0 on the ingest that writes the midx, and 0 on one that does not.
- **Rust, `crates/git/tests/shard.rs`:**
  - `a_miss_on_a_just_moved_tip_or_a_far_chain_is_composed_after_the_catch_up_or_the_step`: an over-the-cap miss starts the step after the running catch-up and composes once the step ends.
  - `a_stuck_catch_up_or_step_ends_at_the_deadline`: a catch-up or step that never ends returns `Late` at the deadline. On main `idle` never returns.
  - `stock_waits_in_arrival_order_within_its_deadline`: places are served in arrival order, and a place past its deadline leaves without holding the ones behind it.
- **Plants:** `tests/b034tails/plant.py`, 13 mutants (over-cap not retried, no step before the compose, the step before the running catch-up ends, no deadline, the line jumped, a non-head asking, a late place kept, no container cap, a slot never freed, ls-refs counted, a far step as a part, every step a base, `midx_ms` dropped); 13 of 13 caught, each by the test named above for its change, and none by a hang or a compile error.

**Flip.** A hosted row where a client waiting for a stock slot fails where a 429 would have let it retry sooner. Or `stockMax` = 2 holding a stock queue past the deadline while the container has memory for more. For option 4, the flip above.

### A 32.20 `MetaSlim` keeps `SLIM_BYTES`; the alarms on slims folded before it are test-install residue, 2026-11-18

**Status.** Recorded on branch `split-refold` from the orchestrator's request (T-01a17bda) to test a split parent's metadata refold before audit-moved. Code-only: one pinning test and one plant. No fold changes.

**Decision.** `MetaSlim` keeps the `SLIM_BYTES` bound (`a0e4d7bc`, 2026-11-14 07:15Z) at format 32.20, with no format of its own for the 512-row rule before it. `crates/git/tests/split.rs`, `a_slim_pass_folds_to_the_digest_its_release_gave`, pins what a slim pass over 1.8 KB rows folds to now (8 slim entries, metadata digest `dd06e4b5…6fac9`), so the next in-place change to `slim` fails in CI. `tests/m0carried/plant40.py` mutant 4, `SLIM_BYTES` reverted, is caught.

**Why.** `a0e4d7bc` changed what an existing 32.20 `MetaSlim` writes in place, the same kind of break as F88: an entry recorded under the 512-row rule slims up to 512 rows, while the same entry replayed on a later release stops at 128 KiB, so the slim cursor and the slimmed rows differ. Measured in memory: a 552-comment slim pass of 1.8 KB rows gives 2 entries and metadata digest `7aa6e61e…` on the merge before it (`9d08d745`) and 8 entries and `dd06e4b5…` after. Replaying the old release's 560-entry log on main gives a third digest, `cd8217e9…`, which neither release's members held. `repo:1048587`, B0-30 smoke 2's parent, slimmed from 05:59 to 06:08Z on 2026-11-14 under the 512-row rule (`tests/am1/results/b030-split.md`, "Smoke 2"), and every audit of it from 18:33Z on alarmed on the metadata tier alone, all three voters agreeing (`decisions/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`, F88). Adding a format now would fix only test chains: no product install has split, and `SPLIT_AT` is 7 GiB.

**What it beat.**
- **A 32.26 `MetaSlim` with the byte bound, and 32.20 back on the 512-row rule.** That matches F88's rule, but the release that recorded B0-30's rerun slims (`repo:1048590`) already ran `SLIM_BYTES` at 32.20, so 32.20 would then refold wrongly for those chains instead. Both behaviours are committed at 32.20, so no gate on the format can restore every member's digest.
- **No pin.** The corpus's single `Split` fixture slims nothing, so it would not catch the next change to `slim`.

**Ruled out.** The split itself does not break the audit. `split.rs`, `a_refold_of_a_split_parent_s_metadata_tier_matches_its_members`, refolds the parent's metadata tier from snapshots before the split, at the seed, mid-pass (begun before slim entries and read after them, through `snap_undo`) and after the pass, each over the log after it, and every one matches the live digest on main.

**Not explained.** `repo:196628` (BF-20's 3.99 GB tier on graft-m1, metadata-tier alarms from 2026-11-16 09:47Z with sites 0 and 2 differing from the refold and site 1 agreeing) has no split. Its tier was seeded by `/bench_seed` (`workers/site/src/snap.rs`, `bench_seed`), which writes rows from no entry with `graftyard_fold::seed`, member by member. A refold restores the seeded rows only through a snapshot, so a member seeded differently from the snapshot's writer, or seeded again after it, disagrees with the refold for good [inference, untested: the per-member seed history is not in the logs read]. It is test state, not a fold rule.

**Evidence.** The two `split.rs` tests above; `plant40.py` 5 of 5; graft-m1 site a Workers Logs, `fold audit mismatch` on `repo:1048587` (from 11-14 18:33Z, at 294 and 300, metadata only) and `repo:196628` (11-16 09:47Z to 11-17 13:47Z, at 2030 and 2036, metadata only).

**Flip.** A product install that splits a chain before `SLIM_BYTES` shipped, which needs a dual-read release; or a split chain on a release with `SLIM_BYTES` throughout whose metadata refold alarms.

### `audit-moved`: the fold audit refolds only a chain that wrote its fold since its last match, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** The fold audit's cron (`workers/site/src/fold_audit.rs`) marks what it found for each chain on its own site's member (`audit_seen`: the refold's index and digests, and whether every voter answered and matched). On a later visit:
1. **Idle.** If the last refold matched and no voter holds an entry since its index that writes the fold (events, an id block, or a stall's lease extension; `crate::load::moved`), each voter's digests at that index are compared with the refold's again, with no refold and no lookup. A chain the audit finds idle starts no election.
2. **Refold until it matches.** If the last refold alarmed, a voter could not answer, a voter moved, or a voter's ring no longer holds the index, the chain goes to its leader as before, which refolds it when its report is a day old. An idle comparison that mismatches alarms and clears the match, so the chain refolds again.
3. **Deleted.** A tombstoned repository (`git::purge::purgeable`) is neither refolded nor compared until its purge; `audit_route` starts no refold for it without `force`.

`scripts/cost.py` prices the refolds of chains that moved ("Fold audit refolds", `AUDIT_ROWS_PER_ROW` 2 [measured], `AUDIT_MOVED_SHARE` 0.3 [guess]): $30, $390, and $482 a month at 50, 300, and 2,000 developers, which moves the default totals to $261, $1,579, and $9,669. The audit was unpriced before. Measured on 2026-11-18 at 620 B of member SQLite per fold row (`ROW_KB` 0.62, K10), the line is $421, $2,517, and $3,110, and the totals $656, $3,726, and $12,463. Since "`refold-stream`" the refold writes no tier table, and the line is $0.01, $1.48, and $9.03.

**Why.** F48's refold replays a chain's entries from its newest snapshot with the current `apply` and compares the result with the digest each voter's `apply` kept. On a chain with no new entry since a matching refold, a new refold replays the same entries from the same snapshot, so it can only repeat the match, at 14 to 27 rows written per entry refolded and up to 118,523 rows a chain (`decisions/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`, K10). On `graft-m3f` (2026-11-18), 40 finished test repositories cost $0.50 in 50 minutes this way, and the audit's own lookups campaigned their leaderless groups, so every visit added a term's no-op on every member. A tombstoned repository is refolded daily for its whole 90-day retention, for rows nothing reads.

**What it gives up.** A refold reads no member's live tier rows, so storage corruption in a member's rows after `apply` was not caught before either: the digest ring holds what `apply` computed, not a rehash of the rows (`crates/fold/src/tier.rs`, `digest_at`; `refold_digest` is the live-row check, run only on demand by `refold_page`). That gap is K11, not this change. What an idle chain does lose is a re-refold on a new release: a release that changes what an already committed entry folds to (F88, and `MetaSlim`'s `SLIM_BYTES`) was found by refolding chains that had matched on the release before. On an idle chain that is now caught only by the golden-digest corpus in CI (`crates/git/tests/fold_corpus.rs`, F88), and on a moved chain by its next refold.

**What it beat.**
- **A refold every day per chain (F48's cadence).** It costs rows in proportion to the chain's size every day whether or not anything changed.
- **The leader's report kept and reused by the leader alone.** The leader is found by a lookup that campaigns a leaderless group, which is the election the idle path avoids; and the leader can change between visits, so the match is kept on the cron's own member, which every visit reads first.
- **Sampling rows instead of refolding.** It checks less than a refold when a chain moved, and nothing that the voters' digests miss when it did not.

**Evidence.** `workers/site/src/load.rs`, `only_an_entry_that_writes_the_fold_moves_a_chain`, and `workers/site/src/fold_audit.rs`, `an_unmoved_chain_is_compared_at_its_last_match_and_not_refolded`; per-object rows written on `graft-m3f` and `graft-m2b` (K10).

**Flip.** A storage-corruption case found on an idle chain by K11's live-row check ("`live-check`") that a daily refold would have found first; a refold of an unmoved chain that disagrees with its last matching report; or a release-time fold change on an idle chain that the corpus missed and a refold would have caught.

### `refold-stream`: the fold audit stages a snapshot as pages and refolds over them, writing no tier table, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** The fold audit's refold (`workers/site/src/load.rs`) no longer restores snapshots into scratch tier tables.
1. **Stage.** Each tier's snapshot is read in 1 MiB ranges, checked frame by frame by `Restore` (order, count, and digest against the trailer, as before), and regrouped by `graftyard_fold::Pager` into pages of at most `PAGE_BYTES` (256 KB [guess]), one row each in `audit_page(tier, tab, last, first, rows) WITHOUT ROWID`. `key_bytes` encodes a key so that comparing the bytes orders keys as `Key` does, so `last >= key ORDER BY last LIMIT 1` finds the only page that can hold it.
2. **Apply.** Each entry applies through `SnapView`, a `Store` over the pages: the batch's own changes in memory, then the changes earlier batches saved in `audit_overlay(tier, tab, k, row) WITHOUT ROWID`, then the page, through a cache of `CACHE_PAGES` (8) decoded pages. `apply` and `Writer` are unchanged. Every read is synchronous and complete: a page not in the cache is read from SQLite then, so no read ever answers "absent" for a row the tier holds. Writes to the digest ring and `snap_undo` tables are dropped, since an audit reads neither.
3. **Commit.** Entries apply only in a batch that staged nothing, so the views read committed pages. A batch's changes are saved with its cursor in one transaction, and a batch stops once a view holds `AUDIT_CHANGES` (20,000) changed rows. An entry's changes therefore reach `audit_overlay` only with the batch that applied it, and a failed batch keeps nothing.
4. **End.** The audit's end deletes every `audit_page` and `audit_overlay` row in the transaction that writes its report. A failed or abandoned audit deletes them with its job. A restored member deletes them unless an audit job is still running (`keeps_audit_rows`), so an object reset between the last batch and the end leaves none behind. A job from an older release, which loads scratch tables, is dropped on its next alarm and refolded at the next due run.
5. **Bound.** An audit stages only when the snapshots fit in half the member's room below `SPLIT_AT` (`stage_fits`), so its own pages never start a split. That replaces `AUDIT_SNAPSHOT_MAX`. A deep audit now also refolds the metadata tier from its newest snapshot and reports both tiers, so `TierLoad.skip` is gone.

The install path is unchanged. `InstallSnapshot` still restores into scratch tables, because those become the member's tiers (`Write::Install`). The audit's scratch branch in `batch`, `finish_audit`'s scratch digest, the audit side of `reset_scratch`, `TierLoad.skip`, `AUDIT_SNAPSHOT_MAX`, `crates/fold`'s old `refold_segment` (restore into an empty store), and `AUDIT_ROWS_PER_ROW` in `scripts/cost.py` are deleted. `refold_segment` now stages and applies through `SnapView`.

`scripts/cost.py` prices the line from what the refold does: pages written and deleted, changed rows (`FOLD_PUTS` per tail entry) saved and deleted, a job row per batch, `AUDIT_FIXED_ROWS` (26) per audit, rows read, one R2 Class B read per MiB of snapshot, and member duration at m3-wp5's 4.7 MB/s. It comes to $0.01, $1.48, and $9.03 a month at 50, 300, and 2,000 developers, against $421, $2,517, and $3,110 for the scratch restore, and to $0.10, $8.02, and $17.10 at the 65 B floor. The default totals are $235, $1,211, and $9,362. Cadence stays daily: the line is at most 0.56% of a total, far under the 10% the orchestrator set for weekly. Since K12's re-price and the fixed rows measured on site day m3frs, the line is $0.01, $2.26, and $9.29 ($0.10, $8.80, and $17.37 at the floor), at most 0.18% of a total.

**Why.** The scratch restore wrote about 2 rows per tier row refolded (K10), 64% to 68% of the bill at 50 and 300 developers. `apply` reads the tier as it writes (`Writer::before_change` for the sum and `snap_undo`, `on_entry`'s expiry scans, and event reads such as the unresolved-thread count), so a refold has to answer reads over the tier as of each entry. Three ways to do that were priced. (A) answered a page not in memory as "absent" and re-applied the entry once the page arrived. That is unsafe: fold code may assert on a row it is entitled to expect. `count_unresolved` panics with "an unresolved count never goes below zero" when `CommentEvent::Resolved` finds its thread and misses its count, and a panic on wasm resets every member in the isolate (`workers/site/src/tier.rs`; F47). Staging makes every read synchronous, so no read can be wrong, at 2 rows per 256 KB page rather than 2 per tier row.

**What it beat.**
- **(A) read-through with a miss and re-apply.** Cheaper by cents ($0.27, $1.58, and $9.68), but unsafe as above.
- **(B) streaming only the tiers or event kinds that never read during apply.** Nothing qualifies: `on_entry` scans an expiry head in both tiers on every entry, and every write reads the old row.
- **(C) scratch tables without billed writes.** workerd's authorizer refuses `CREATE TEMP TABLE` and `ATTACH` (`src/workerd/util/sqlite.c++`), and every row written to a table is billed. `WITHOUT ROWID` scratch tables would halve the line to 14% to 51% of the total.
- **Weekly cadence for moved chains.** Saves cents once the line is cents.

**Evidence.**
- `crates/git/tests/fold_corpus.rs`, `every_committed_event_refolds_through_staged_pages_to_the_same_digests`: all 48 kinds at every format, 902 rows, staged with a snapshot after the setup entry, fold to the golden digests.
- Refold against restore at every index (`fold_digest`, `refold_digest`, and every row), with pages of a few rows read through a cache of one page:
  - `repo:65536`'s shape scaled down (`crates/git/tests/refold_stream.rs`): 360 refs, 180 leases, 150 checks, and review threads, then a tail that moves refs, renews leases, resolves and reopens threads, promotes, prunes leases across pages, and expires every check.
  - The split parent from snapshots before the split, at the seed, mid-pass, and after the pass (`split.rs`, `a_refold_of_a_split_parent_s_metadata_tier_matches_its_members`).
  - The 552-comment slim (`a_staged_refold_through_a_slim_pass_equals_a_restore_at_every_index`).
- **Pages per entry.** At `PAGE_BYTES` the most pages any one entry of these fixtures read is 4 per tier, and 73 at 300-byte pages. A corpus fixture fits one page per table.
- `key_bytes`' order against `Key`'s over random keys with integers at and across the sign boundary, empty and prefix text and blobs, and the escape byte (`stream::tests`). The same SQL in SQLite itself, for zero- to three-column keys (`crates/fold/tests/stream_sqlite.rs`).
- `an_audits_staged_rows_go_at_its_end_and_on_a_restore_without_it` and `an_audit_stages_only_within_half_the_room_below_split_at` (`workers/site/src/load.rs`).
- `tests/m0carried/plant44.py`: 9 of 9 caught. The mutants: no sign flip on integers; no escape in text; a lookup one page late; a delete that does not hide its page row; a scan short by its deletes; a saved change losing to its page; staging without the trailer check; an end that keeps its pages; a restore that keeps them with no audit.
- Hosted on `graft-m3f`'s site day m3frs (main `7b576074`, 2026-11-18; `tests/am1/results/lm1-rows-m3f.md`, "Site day m3frs"). Two streamed refolds of `repo:65588` matched all three voters on both tiers, and the leader wrote 60 and 52 rows for reports of 6 pages + 11 saved and 6 pages + 14 saved [measured]. That is more than twice `pages + saved` (34 and 40), which is this entry's flip line as written. The excess is not per row: each page and saved change is written and deleted once by design, which `cost.py` prices, and the remaining 12 to 26 rows are fixed per audit (`load_job` per batch, `load_report`, `audit_seen`, and in one minute a new term's no-ops) [inference]. At 1,824 to 10,506 refolds a month that adds $0.02 to $0.27, so the line stays under 1% of every total. The orchestrator ruled the flip not tripped, and it is reworded below so a fixed per-audit cost cannot trip it; `cost.py` prices those rows as `AUDIT_FIXED_ROWS` 26.
- audit-moved on the same day: the cron's own pass found `repo:65588` `idle` after its matched refold (no refold, no lookup), and `deleted` after its `DELETE` (204) [measured].

**Flip.** A hosted refold whose `rowsWritten` is more than 2 × (pages + changed rows) it reports plus a fixed per-audit allowance of 26 rows, set from site day m3frs's 12 to 26 (the job, report and `audit_seen` rows, and a no-op entry in the same minute), or a fixture or chain where the staged refold and a restore give different digests. Also, staging costs that pass 10% of a total at some tier, for example a snapshot-per-row size far below 65 B.

### `audit-cover`: a fold-audit run spends its samples on live chains only, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** Each cron run of the fold audit (`workers/site/src/fold_audit.rs`, `walk`) looks at this site's homed registry rows from its cursor until it has audited `SAMPLE` (4) chains or looked at `LOOK_MAX` (64) rows, each row at most once a run. A row costs a look and no sample when it is `retired`, `deleted`, or `skipped` (a probe or non-repository group). `retired` means this site's member answers 409 "member not joined" and so does every other site's member that its registry row names, asked directly, so no lookup and no election starts. The cursor moves to the last row looked at, and the report counts `retired`.

**Why.** On `graft-m3f`'s site day m3frs (2026-11-18), site a's registry homed 53 chains (`repo:65536` to `65588`), none of them joined after the close-out; sites b and c homed none of them. The six crons from 18:18 to 19:33Z each spent all 4 samples on retired test chains 65536 to 65547 and never reached a live one [measured, `tests/am1/results/lm1-rows-m3f.md`, "Site day m3frs"]. The rows stay because the test route `/retire` (`workers/site/src/member.rs`) deletes the member's storage and resets it, standing for a lost member (BF-11's `ReplaceMember`), whose registry row must stay for its replacement; and `tests/fanout/purge.py` deletes bucket objects only. The product purge does delete each site's row (`workers/edge/src/purge.rs`, `unregister`), but between a repository's delete and its purge its rows stay as `deleted`, and those also took samples. So the cursor, not retire or purge, is where a stale or tombstoned row has to stop costing coverage.

**What it beat.**
- **Deleting the registry row from `/retire`.** It would break the lost-member case `/retire` stands for, and it leaves `deleted` rows taking samples in production.
- **Deleting a row found not joined everywhere.** A registry write from the audit on evidence from one pass; a lost home slot answers 409 on its home too, and the other sites' answers are what tell the two apart. Left to purge, which owns the row.
- **A larger `SAMPLE`.** Every run's refolds and voter calls grow with it, and a site of mostly retired rows still starves.

**Evidence.** `a_run_over_mostly_retired_rows_still_audits_the_live_ones` (`workers/site/src/fold_audit.rs`): 30 rows of which 5 live, from a cursor, wrapping, and 200 retired rows bounded by `LOOK_MAX`. It fails on main's rule (every look a sample): no live chain reached.

**Flip.** A run whose looks pass `LOOK_MAX` before it audits `SAMPLE` live chains on a real install, so live chains go unaudited for days: then purge deletes rows the audit finds retired everywhere, or the registry keeps live and tombstoned rows apart.

### `k12-rows`: member rows written priced at 17 an entry; tier tables stay without `WITHOUT ROWID`, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** `scripts/cost.py` prices a member's rows written per entry as `ENTRY_ROWS` 17: each fold row put counted twice (the tier table's rowid table and its key's automatic index), `log` 1, `request` 2, and `raft_state` 1 or 2. The audit's changed rows stay `FOLD_PUTS` 6 an entry, because `audit_overlay` is `WITHOUT ROWID`. `cost_agents.py`'s learners and grant entries use `ENTRY_ROWS`, and its PathSet and provenance puts count 2 rows each. The tier tables keep their schema: moving them to `WITHOUT ROWID` is deferred.

**Why.** K12's measurement: one `DefineLabel` entry, 6 fold puts, wrote 19 rows on the leader in each of 4 quiet minutes, 2 of them test-only (`arrival` and `sqlite_sequence`) [measured, `graft-m3f` site day m3frs, `tests/am1/results/lm1-rows-m3f.md`]. workerd counts a row for each `OP_Insert` and each `OP_IdxInsert` (`patches/sqlite/0001-row-counts-plain.patch` in cloudflare/workerd [doc]). The rows-written line moves from $0, $0, and $270 to $0, $66, and $726 a month at 50, 300, and 2,000 developers, and the totals to $235, $1,280, and $9,819 (agent layer $21, $330, and $2,947).

**What it beat.** `WITHOUT ROWID` tier tables now: a new tier table set and a refold of every member (`design/SHARED.md`, "Schema change is a refold, never a migration") to save about $66 and $726 a month, under 8% of any total.

**Evidence.** As above; the leader's minute-by-minute `rowsWritten` per object from `durableObjectsPeriodicGroups`.

**Flip.** The rows-written line passes 10% of a total at some tier, or another change already forces a new tier table set and a refold, in which case `WITHOUT ROWID` rides along.

**Flip fired, 2026-11-19.** The orchestrator (T-01a17bda) ruled that "a total" counts the agent layer, which ships with the product. At 2,000 developers the rows-written line is $726 base plus $574 agents, $1,301 of $12,802, 10.2% (`python3 scripts/cost_agents.py`, main `330693e6`). `WITHOUT ROWID` tier tables are accepted, 11 rows an entry for this one in place of 17, saving $486 a month at 2,000 developers and $73 at 300 (`cost_agents.py --levers`, `without-rowid`, branch `cost-levers`). They are queued behind the AM1 load rows, because the new table set ships with a refold of every member on a site day, and are not built yet. Its gate: one `DefineLabel` writes 13 rows on the leader (11 product, 2 test-only), against 19 today.

**Flip withdrawn, 2026-11-19 (re-priced by family and kind).** The 10.2% came from charging every entry the 17 rows a repository `DefineLabel` writes. Counted per statement in local workerd (`rows_written()`, the meter Cloudflare bills) with the member's own `tier.rs` statements and DDL, `bash tests/entryrows/run.sh` [measured]:
- A repository entry writes its fold-tier rows, which run from 6 (`Refused`) to 23 (`PrOpened`), FTS5 rows included: a `Refs` push 10, a `Comment` 16, a PrSync round (`Refs`, `TestMerged`, `ConsumerCursor`) 16, an agent push (`Refs`, `Provenance`, `PathSet`) 14. On top of those it writes `request` 3 (the table, the `rid` index, and `request_at`), `log` 1 and `raft_state` 1 per input, and later 2 deletes (its `request` row expired, its `log` row truncated after archive).
- The bed's `DefineLabel` writes 14 (fold 9: `_fold` and `ids` are rowid aliases and write 1 each), which matches graft-m3f's hosted 15 on followers and 19 on the leader once `raft_state`'s second write and the leader's test-only `arrival` row (3 rows: its table, `arrival_at`, `sqlite_sequence`) are added [measured, K12].
- An Actions, Identity, Tokens, Names, Authz or Ids entry writes its whole fold as one `fold` row (a rowid alias): 8.3 rows with the host's rows and its expiry.

Repository entries average 21.7 rows per member, but 85% of entries at every tier are Actions and Identity entries (`cost.py` `workload`: 12.8 M of 15.2 M a month at 2,000 developers). `scripts/cost.py` now prices `REPO_KIND_ROWS` by kind, with ACTIVITY's metadata writes on `META_MIX` [guess] and the agent layer's writes on their own kinds (`cost_agents.py`, `meta_kinds`). Rows written are $0, $20 and $420 a month in the base and $0, $84 and $563 in the agent layer; base totals $236, $1,013 and $9,323, with agents $257, $1,341 and $12,254. Base plus agent rows written, with the PathSet and provenance line, is $993 of $12,254 at 2,000 developers (8.1%) and $107 of $1,341 at 300 (7.9%): under 10%, so this entry's flip no longer holds. The `WITHOUT ROWID` build is withdrawn ("`without-rowid`").

### `live-check`: each voter rehashes its tier rows weekly against the sum `apply` kept, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** The fold audit's cron sends each voter it visits `/fold {"live": true}` beside its digest reads, on both the refold and the idle path (`workers/site/src/fold_audit.rs`). The voter answers its last live-row check and starts one when the last is `LIVE_EVERY_MS` (7 days [guess]) old (`workers/site/src/live.rs`). A check is a snapshot job with no upload (`SnapshotJob::live_step`, `crates/fold/src/snapshot.rs`): `begin` marks each tier's `to` in turn, the member's alarm reads `ROWS_PER_READ` (500) rows at a time for at most `BATCH_MS` (2 s) through `snap_undo`, and the trailer's rehash of every row as of `to` is compared with `want`, the sum `apply` kept. Then `end_snapshot` drops the copies. Nothing is uploaded or committed. The result is kept in `live_last`; a mismatch logs "fold live-row mismatch" with the chain, site and tier, and the cron report counts `liveStarted` and `liveAlarms`. It does not clear the refold's `matched`, since a refold reads no live row. Repair is the operator's (`ReplaceMember`), never automatic. Voters only; learners are F93.

Conditions the orchestrator set before code:
1. **Duration bound.** At m2-wp1's 1,200 rows/s through `snap_undo` [measured, `tests/m2/results/m2-wp1.md`], `repo:65536`'s 571,889-row core tier takes 7.9 min and BF-20's 3.99 GB, 1.33 M-row metadata tier 18.5 min, both tiers in turn. `apply` keeps at most one `snap_undo` copy per row the tier held at `to`, so the copies never pass the tier's row count; BF-20's own snapshot under 300 commands/s held its undo through 196 entries. On a busy chain they could still reach the row count, so the check counts them before each batch (`TierSql::undo_rows`, one statement) and ends as `abandoned` past `LIVE_UNDO_MAX` (50,000 copies, about 31 MB at 620 B a row [guess]). The next due visit tries again.
2. **No added latency.** It reads at the snapshot writer's `ROWS_PER_READ` and `BATCH_MS`, and yields between reads. A visit starts none while the member leads with commands queued (`admitted_bytes` above 0), while a snapshot job or mark or a refold or install job runs, while a split parent slims, or while its metadata tier is unloaded or dropped (`live::may_start`). A real snapshot that comes due on the same tier takes it: the check ends as `yielded` (`yield_to_snapshot`), and an install that replaces a tier ends it as `gone` (`SnapshotJob::holds`), with no verdict either way.
3. **The failing-on-main test** (`crates/fold/tests/tiers.rs`, `a_row_changed_in_storage_after_apply_is_caught_by_the_live_check_alone`): a metadata row overwritten in the store with no entry. `fold_digest`, the digest ring at `to`, and a refold of the log all still give the kept digest; the live check, run while later entries change, delete and add rows past `to`, names the metadata tier, and the clean core tier matches.

`scripts/cost.py` prices it as "Fold live-row check, weekly per voter (K11)": every voter's tier rows read once a week, member duration at 1,200 rows/s, and the `snap_undo` copies of the fold puts made during each scan, put and deleted. $0.76, $4.31, and $35.52 a month at 50, 300, and 2,000 developers; $7, $41, and $339 at the 65 B floor. The default totals move to $236, $1,284, and $9,855.

**Why.** Before this, the snapshot writer was the only live-row check: one non-leader voter, rotating by `to`, only when a snapshot came due, so the leader and idle chains were never checked, and Workers Logs on 12 site scripts from 11-12 to 11-18 held no "trailer digest" failure [measured]. `audit-moved`'s first flip (corruption on an idle chain) could not fire.

**What it beat.**
- **A cron of `refold_page`.** It restarts whenever `applied` moves, so it never finishes on a busy chain.
- **The writer's check alone (today's).** It never reaches leaders or idle chains.
- **An automatic reinstall on a mismatch.** A wrong verdict would reset a healthy member; the operator decides.
- **Learners too.** The cron has no learner names without a lookup; F94.

**Evidence.** The test above fails on main (no live check exists). `live::tests` (`a_check_starts_only_on_a_quiet_member_a_week_after_the_last`, `the_cron_reads_a_voters_mismatching_tiers_from_its_last_check`). `tests/m0carried/plant47.py`: 8 of 8 caught. The mutants: comparing the trailer with itself; a verdict on a tier an install replaced; reading live rows without `snap_undo`; abandoning at the cap, not past it; starting while the leader holds queued commands, while a snapshot runs, or at every visit; and a cron that reads no mismatch. The hosted half rides the next `graft-m3f` site day: a `liveStarted` count, one voter's `live_last`, and its rows read.

**Flip.** A hosted check that is abandoned on most busy chains (then scan faster or cap by time), or that moves a leader's commit p99 while it reads (then start it only on followers); a mismatch found on a chain whose members' snapshots all match a refold (then the check, not the rows, is wrong); or the line passing 10% of a total.

### `shed-backoff`: a write's shed read backs off and gives up after `SHED_RETRY_FOR`, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** `graftyard_lookup::retry_shed` waits after the nth shed pass in a row `OVERLOAD_RETRY_MS` (250 ms) doubled per pass up to `SHED_BACKOFF_MAX_MS` (2 s), with a random part of up to half taken off, and never under the `retryAfterMs` the members named. The edge gives a write `SHED_RETRY_FOR` (4 s [guess]) in place of LOOKUP_FOR (20 s), and a bounded push the smaller of that and what is left of its AGENT_PUSH_BOUND (`workers/edge/src/lib.rs`, `shed_retry_for`). Past it the write answers 503 with `Retry-After: 1`, or `ng` for an Agent push, as before. Read-class requests still answer at once. This amends `lease-clock` (2), whose flip it meets.

**Why.** `lease-clock` (2)'s flip: "A hosted row where writes wait out `LOOKUP_FOR` on shed reads often enough to move their p99". B0-33 m51 did. After its leader change, 4,200 REST and GraphQL writes answered 503 after 19 to 24 s (p50 22.0 s, every one at least 19 s), each asking the learners again every 250 ms. The 4 learners' reads rose from 15 to 54 a second each to 136, 476, 486 and 514, 85 to 90% whole-tier reads, and the row ended with 18,294 × 5xx [measured, Workers Logs and trace, `tests/am1/results/c-design.md`, "B0-33 with 4 learners, m51"]. With every pass shed, a held write now makes 2 to 5 passes, not 7 to 80, and has its answer by about 4 s plus one pass.

**Beat.** Keeping LOOKUP_FOR with backoff alone: 12 tries a write in 20 s, still a multiplier, and the 503 still at 20 s. A fixed shorter deadline without backoff: still a pass every 250 ms while it lasts, and every write shed together comes back together. Sending a write's shed read to the leader after its deadline: the overflow that stepped leaders down on every 500-agent row ("Follower read").

**Evidence.** `a_read_the_members_keep_shedding_backs_off_and_gives_up` and `a_shed_read_is_retried_inside_its_deadline_only` (`crates/lookup/src/lib.rs`), and `a_write_asks_a_shed_read_again_for_seconds_not_lookup_for` (`workers/edge/src/lib.rs`), which fail on main. `tests/m0carried/plant43.py`. `tests/am1/results/health-gate-lease.md`, item 2.

**Amended** by `shed-retry-2s` (2026-11-19): `SHED_RETRY_FOR` is 2 s.

**Flip.** A hosted row where writes behind the read gate answer 503 after SHED_RETRY_FOR during a stall that ended within LOOKUP_FOR often enough to fail a gate line on 5xx share, with the learners' read rate not over twice the clients' while it lasts: then the retry budget, not the multiplier, is the cost.

### `lease-gone`: a renew whose lease a release in its entry removed answers 404, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** `leases::render_ok` (`crates/api/src/leases.rs`) answers 404 for a committed lease command whose row is gone by render time, as `refused` does for `LeaseErr::NotFound`, in place of 500 `no lease row`.

**Why.** The reply renders over tiers that have applied the whole entry, so a renew followed by a release of the same lease in that entry finds no row. On B0-33 m50 all 157 lease-renew 500s were renews with a release (204) of the same lease in flight, while 2,881 renews of an already-released lease answered 404 [measured, Workers Logs, `tests/am1/results/c-design.md`, "m50's 943 5xx, attributed"]. The renew did commit; to the client the lease is gone either way.

**Beat.** Rendering the renew from the row as `decide` saw it: the reply would describe a lease that no longer exists, and `render_ok` reads only the applied tiers.

**Evidence.** `a_renew_whose_lease_a_release_in_its_entry_removed_answers_404` (`crates/api/tests/lease_api.rs`) fails on main with 500. `tests/m0carried/plant43.py`.

**Flip.** A client that needs the renewed expiry of a lease another request released in the same entry.

### `stale-log`: each push of a load run is logged on both sides, and a `Stale` is judged against its ref's previous push, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** `tests/am1/rest/a1.mjs` writes one row per push to `tests/am1/raw/a1-pushes-<row>-<run>.jsonl`: a client push id, the kind, the ref, the old and new tips, the reply's `x-github-request-id`, the result or error, and start and end on Cloudflare's clock (`tests/fanout/srvclock.mjs`). It sends the id as `x-graft-client-push`. A test edge writes the id, if it is at most 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, into its push line, beside `end`, the leader's answer: the index and each ref's outcome, or the refusal, `full`, `notLeader`, or the call error (`workers/edge/src/lib.rs`, `push_log`, `client_push_id`). A product edge reads neither. `tests/fanout/stalecheck.mjs` judges each `stale` against the ref's previous push. It fails the run when that push was acked `ok` at the tip the `stale` named, or refused while leaving the ref at that tip. It passes a lost reply that the edge shows committed `Ok`, and an overlap with another push to the ref (a race). It reports the rest as UNKNOWN.

**Why.** B0-29's "zero `Stale` on distinct refs" is an invariant line: a `Stale` with no cause would be the group moving a ref nobody was told about. Run 6 had 1 agent `stale` in 2,500 pushes, and its records could not say which push moved the ref. The edge's lines then held no ref and no per-ref outcome, and the driver kept only counts. The counts did rule out the obvious cause: 2,816 push lines at the edge, all 200, against 2,865 pushes sent, so the 49 client `fetch failed` never reached the edge [measured, `tests/am1/results/b029-m2b.md`, "Run 6"].

**Beat.** Logging the ref in the edge line alone: a lost reply has no client row to join it to. Asking the leader's `request` rows after the run: the network is retired and purged by close-out, and the rows hold events, not the client's view.

**Evidence.** `tests/fanout/stalecheck.test.mjs` (3 tests); `ls_refs_go_to_the_shard_only_when_a_bed_request_asks` (`workers/edge/src/lib.rs`) for the id filter; `tests/m0carried/plant45.py`, 8 of 8 caught.

**Flip.** A run whose per-push log and edge lines disagree on a push's outcome (the edge line `Ok` with the client row `ok` for another commit), which would mean the join is wrong.

### F91's A/B switch: `x-graft-ls-refs: shard` with the bed token, test installs only, 2026-11-18

**Decision.** A test-faults edge answers a v2 `ls-refs` from the group's refs (`b034-reads`) unless the request carries `x-graft-ls-refs: shard` with the bed token. Then the request goes to the shard, as before `b034-reads` (`ls_refs_at_edge`, `Ctx::ls_refs_edge`). The switch is on by default, and a product edge has no switch. a1.mjs's `--ls-refs-shard` adds the header to every upload-pack. So F91's A/B is one edge build from one main: run 7 with the flag against run 6 without it.

**Why.** F91 asks whether the leader's refs pages set run 6's commit p99. Run 6 differed from run 5 in 17 merges, so only an arm that turns off only the edge's `ls_refs` answers it (operator, 2026-11-18).

**Beat.** An edge variable: it changes only by deploying the edge again, and the A/B would need two edge deploys. A header that any client could send: it would let a product request choose the leader's work.

**Evidence.** `ls_refs_go_to_the_shard_only_when_a_bed_request_asks` (`workers/edge/src/lib.rs`); `tests/m0carried/plant45.py` mutants 5 and 6.

**Flip.** F91 answered either way: then the switch goes with whichever path wins.

### `extend-floor`: the leader stamps no `ExtendLeases` under `EXTEND_MIN` (2 s), 2026-11-18

**Decision.** The leader's `take_extend` (`crates/raft/src/member/leader.rs`) stamps no `extend` when `by` is under `EXTEND_MIN` (2 s [guess]: four `DRIFT`s, above run 7's healthy round and cycle p99s of 325 and 413 ms). The marker then clears as before, when a later-stamped entry commits (`set_commit`). `by` still runs from `since`, the later of the marker and the last entry's `at`, so the floor applies to the whole stall and not to its last gap. Path leases (`crates/git/src/lease.rs`, `extend`) and Actions job leases (`crates/actions/src/shard.rs`, `extended`) both read only an entry's `extend`, so one rule covers both with no change to either fold.

**Why.** On B0-33 m52 an `ExtendLeases` rewrote every live lease at 3 statements each, about 1,365 statements a firing and 46% of the leader's deferred statements, and the leader confirmed those transactions at p50 545 ms against a follower's 24 ms [measured, `tests/am1/results/tx-mix.md`]. The stalls that fired them were 0.06 to 4.6 s. At 2 s the floor drops 7 of 11, 11 of 16 and 8 of 12 of them on the three leaders that fired often (64 to 69%) [measured, `tests/am1/results/write-cuts.md`, "Cut 2 at 2 s"]. The cost is slack: every sub-floor stall moves no lease, so a lease that is not renewed lapses earlier by the sum of sub-floor stalls since its last renewal, about 20 to 78 s per 600 s TTL at those leaders' rates, and then at its wall-clock `expires`, as on an idle group [inference]. A holder that renews is unaffected.

**Beat.** A floor in `lease::extend`, where the extension is applied: entries already committed with a sub-floor `extend` would fold differently after the upgrade, which breaks F88's rule that a committed entry folds the same on every build, and `fold_corpus` builds every fixture with `extend: None`, so it would not catch it. Gating that floor by the entry's `format`: `extend` rides `Noop`, config and id-block entries at `RAFT_FORMAT`, and `on_extend` does not see the format. `EXTEND_MIN` of 5 s: it removed every `ExtendLeases` on these rows and cost up to 211 s of a 600 s TTL (operator, 2026-11-18). A different rule for Actions job leases: SHARED says they move by the same rule, and nothing in a job lease's use differs.

**Evidence.** `crates/raft/tests/scenarios.rs`, `a_stall_under_extend_min_stamps_no_extend_and_clears_its_marker` and `a_quick_campaign_after_idle_time_stamps_no_extend`; `crates/git/tests/lease_gates.rs`, `repeated_stalls_under_extend_min_leave_an_unrenewed_lease_at_its_wall_clock_expires` (three 1.5 s stalls leave an unrenewed lease at its granted `expires`, then a 3 s stall moves it by 3 s); `crates/actions/tests/gates.rs`, `a_job_lease_moves_only_for_a_stall_of_extend_min`, the same for a job lease. Each fails on main. `tests/writecuts/plant2.py`, 4 of 4 caught: `>` for `>=`, the floor on the last gap instead of the stall from `since`, the marker kept after a dropped stamp, and no floor. The long sweep and Porcupine on `hist.jsonl` and `hist.jsonl.gray` (`tests/am1/results/write-cuts.md`).

**Flip.** A measured lease handoff that a sub-floor stall made wrong (a second holder granted overlapping Exclusive scope while the first was renewing on schedule), or a holder-visible early lapse on a renewing holder.

### F91: the edge's `ls-refs` reads its refs from learners and followers, 2026-11-18

**Status.** Built on branch `f91-follower-refs` from main `cc8d1861`, design approved by the orchestrator (T-01a17bda). Edge and site code, so it ships on a combined site day; F91 closes when B0-29 run 8 passes on it.

**Decision.** The edge answers a v2 `ls-refs` from one read, `{"lsRefs": {"reads": [..], "head": bool}}` (`LsRefs::query`), which a member answers from its own fold alone: HEAD's `default_branch` and tip from the `settings` row and that ref, and one page per read (`graftyard_git::ls_refs::read`). The edge sends it by read-index to the group's learners first, then its followers (`graftyard_lookup::read_off_leader`), and `follower_query` admits it with no `meta_loaded` gate, since it reads the core tier only. If every member asked sheds it, declines it, or fails, the read returns nothing and the shard answers, never the leader. `LsRefs::answer_read` refuses an answer whose HEAD tip differs from its branch's line, which one fold never gives. receive-pack's advertisement and every other paged refs read stay on the leader. The query code `lsRefs` is appended to `READ_QUERIES`. Two cases still reach the leader, both as `read_spread`'s other reads do: an edge isolate that knows no leader yet asks any voter, and one that leads serves the read itself; and a member built before this change declines the read, so the request goes to the shard until the site day carries it.

**Freshness.** An `ls-refs` after a push must list that push, as GHES's does: read-your-writes for an acknowledged push. A learner's or follower's read-index answer gives it: the member asks the leader for its commit index, which the leader confirms by lease or round, and is granted only once it has applied that index (`raft::ReadGrant::floor`), so its fold holds every entry acknowledged before the read arrived ("Follower read"). One read answers HEAD and every page, so the answer is one state: two reads, even at or above the same floor, can land on either side of an apply.

**Why.** F91: on B0-29 run 6 the leader served 36 refs pages a second beside its commit path, and its round p99 rose to 2,353 ms and commit p99 to 7,720 ms. Run 7, with only the edge's `ls-refs` off, took the leader's refs pages to 0, round p99 to 325 ms and commit p99 to 817 ms, and API reads served from 86.7% to 100% [measured, `tests/am1/results/b029-m2b.md`, runs 6 and 7]. At run 6's rate the pages move to 8 learners, about 4.5 a second each [inference].

**What it beat.**
- **Pages on the leader (`b034-reads`).** That is F91's cause.
- **One read per page through `read_spread`, with HEAD's `settings` read beside them, and a check that every read's index is at or above HEAD's.** Two reads at or above one floor can still answer from two states: a page read before an apply and HEAD read after it give one answer from two folds (operator, 2026-11-18). Requiring equal indexes across reads works but sheds more answers to the shard on a busy group, where indexes move between calls; one read needs no check.
- **`read_spread` with its fall-through to the leader.** A read every learner and follower declines (a group whose learners are not placed, a member that knows no leader) would put the pages back on the leader. The shard served `ls-refs` before `b034-reads`, so it stays the fallback.

**Evidence.** `crates/git/tests/ls_refs.rs`: `a_follower_ls_refs_after_an_acknowledged_push_lists_the_new_tip` (three real `Member<RepoCmd>`s; a push acknowledged without one follower, then an `ls-refs` read on that follower whose read-index answer arrives before its entries: the read waits, and is answered at or above the push with the new tip in HEAD and in its branch's line); `head_and_its_branch_from_two_states_go_to_the_shard`. `workers/site/src/fanout.rs`, `a_follower_serves_only_the_designs_reads`. `tests/m0carried/plant46.py`: a follower granted at its own applied index (below its floor), a two-state answer passed, HEAD left out of the read, and a follower that declines the read. Hosted: B0-29 run 8 moved the refs reads off the leader (0 ls-refs and 0 refs pages on it, 34.9/s on the learners). The within-network control (row `m2bb29n`, 2026-11-19) switched the edge's `ls-refs` between this path and the shard every minute on one network, so placement was fixed: the leader's confirm p50 paired by minute was +1.0 ms edge minus shard over 4 pairs, the edge-side API time was the same in both arms (graphql p50 249 and 237 ms), and no member shared an isolate with the leader [measured, `tests/am1/results/b029-m2b.md`, "The within-network control"]. The slower leaders on run 8 and the A-B-A's F91 row were their networks' placement (1-statement setup confirm 38–39 ms against 19–21 on the shard rows), so co-locating the leader with the learners that serve `ls-refs` is not a cost of this choice, and the off-site preference named after the A-B-A is not built.

**Flip.** A learner's `ls-refs` answer that shows a ref older than a push acknowledged to the client before the request (a per-push log row from `stale-log` against the same ref's ls-refs line); or the learners' read p99 or shed rate rising past `FOLLOWER_WAIT` with the pages on them, so `ls-refs` goes to the shard more often than it did before `b034-reads`.

### `gh-token`: a job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, M4-WP3 slice B, 2026-11-18

**Status.** Approved by the lead (T-01a17bda) as slice B of M4-WP3, code-only, on branch `gh-token`. It needs a site day that ships the readers of formats 0x15.5 and 0x12.14 to every member, `FormatsEnable` of both, then a site day and an edge day that set `GRAFTYARD_JOB_TOKENS=1` on the sites. None is run for it alone; the runner account stays idle until a site day carries slices A and B together.

**Decision.**
- **Identity.** A job's token is an ordinary stateless installation token (`ghs_`) of the install-owned Actions App, `ACTIONS_APP` (id 2 of cell 0's block 0, which `Ids` never leases), installed on each owner. Its installation id is the owner's id negated (`actions_installation`), and its row is `actions_row()`: every repository, every GHES `GITHUB_TOKEN` scope at write. The token itself names only the run's repository and the job's permissions, and `authorize` takes the lower of claims and row, so the row is only a ceiling.
- **Installed at the first `acquirejob`, not the first `RunCreated`.** The edge reads the owner's `Authz` during the acquire anyway (it names the repository), commits `AuthzOp::Install` under the operator credential when the row is missing, and only then mints. `Install` of the Actions App reads no dep (`AuthzCmd::deps` skips it), and `ActionsOp`'s deps stay empty, so `decide` gains no dependency on either chain. Committing it with `RunCreated` would have made the Actions shard's `decide` read or write an `Authz` chain, a cross-group dep that `CreateRun` does not have today. A second install of the same row writes nothing, so two racing acquires are safe.
- **The id never collides and is never listed.** `Ids` assigns only positive ids, and `RegisterInstallation` refuses an id ≤ 0 (`Reserved`), so no real installation takes a negative one, and `Install` accepts the Actions App only at `actions_installation(owner)` with `actions_row()` (`BadRecord` otherwise). `Uninstall` of a negative id is `Forbidden`. The installation has no `Names` route, so `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` answers 404 for it, and the App has no `AppRecord`, so no App JWT verifies for it and `hookseq::read_owner_apps` delivers it nothing. The edge serves no installation-listing route (`/orgs/{org}/installations`, `/user/installations`, `/repos/{o}/{r}/installation`, `/app/installations` are all unrouted and answer as they did), so no GHES 3.22 response changes for a non-Actions client [inference from the edge's route table; GHES itself documents `github-actions` under no installation route].
- **Lifetime.** `job_token_life(JOB_LIMIT, JOB_LEASE)`: 360 minutes, GHES's default `timeout-minutes`, plus one 10-minute lease, capped at `JOB_TOKEN_MAX` (24 h). `Grant.lifetime_ms` carries it to `graft-ops`, whose `mint` caps it at `max_lifetime(app)`, and `verify` refuses any token whose `exp - iat` exceeds that, so only the Actions App's tokens outlive `INSTALLATION_TOKEN_TTL` (1 h). Every other installation token keeps 1 h.
- **The jti deny is the real bound.** `job_jti(job, attempt)` derives the `jti`, so nothing stores it. `AcquireToken` (format 0x15.5) commits `Acquired` plus `TokenIssued` in one entry, and the shard leader puts the token in the job message only from such an entry. `RunOwner` reads each entry after its cursor, and for every issued job that a `Finished`, `Cancel` or `LeaseExpired` completed it commits `RevokeJti` on the `jti`'s `Tokens` shard, with `exp` 24 h past the end, before the shard half that moves its cursor. A repository's deletion cancels its runs (`RunOwner`'s `Gone` path), which is a `Cancel`. A crash repeats the round from the same cursor and its content-derived request ids commit nothing twice.
- **Permissions follow GHES.** The default, then the workflow's `permissions:`, then the job's, any of which may grant above the default; a scope a mapping leaves out is `none`; for a pull request from a fork every write becomes read [doc: GHES 3.22, "Workflow syntax for GitHub Actions", `permissions`]. This replaces the earlier "only narrows" call, as the lead ruled: wire compatibility wins. The default is GHES's restricted one (`contents`, `packages` read) until a `default_workflow_permissions` setting exists (F93). Declared permissions ride `CreateRunWith` (0x15.5) as `JobTokens` beside `RunCreated`.
- **Rotation.** A key retires at the switch plus `SIGNING_KEY_CACHE` plus `JOB_TOKEN_MAX` plus `CLOCK_SKEW`, so a 24 h job token signed by an isolate's cached old key verifies until it expires. The publish-before-sign wait stays one `INSTALLATION_TOKEN_TTL`, because a token is verified against a key that was published before it was signed whatever its lifetime.
- **Order.** Ship the readers (0x15.5 in `Actions::reads`, 0x12.14 in `Authz::reads`) on a site day, `FormatsEnable` both, then set `GRAFTYARD_JOB_TOKENS=1`. The edge mints only once both formats are enabled, and a site sends 0x15.5 only where `GRAFTYARD_JOB_TOKENS` is set.

**What it beat.**
- **A new App per owner registered through `Names`.** It would put an Actions installation in every installation listing and route, a GHES-visible change.
- **Storing each token's `jti` on the job.** A write per acquire and per retry; the derived `jti` needs only the one `TokenIssued` mark, which also keeps a job that never received a token from costing a deny.
- **Denying in the shard's own `decide`.** `RevokeJti` lives on a `Tokens` chain, so it would be a cross-group write from `decide`; `RunOwner` already commits to other chains before its cursor.
- **A 1 h token refreshed by the runner.** The runner has no refresh path for `github.token`; GHES's own token is one installation token for the job.
